why: 5 catalog results name it (e.g. Affine communication lemma, Gabriel-Rosenberg theorem); nLab page 'scheme' has 185 backlinks; Mathlib defines it as AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme. Inference: the foundation of modern algebraic geometry; the bare word 'scheme' has numerical and everyday senses, so only qualified phrases are listed.

name: 3-manifold
def: A topological space that is locally homeomorphic to three-dimensional Euclidean space.
why: 8 catalog results name it (e.g. Bing's recognition theorem, Lickorish–Wallace theorem); nLab page '3-manifold' has 41 backlinks. Inference: a central object of geometric topology.

name: Algebraic number
def: A complex number that is a root of a nonzero polynomial with rational coefficients.
why: 8 catalog results name it (e.g. Baker's theorem, Gelfond's theorem); nLab page 'algebraic number' has 20 backlinks; Mathlib defines it as IsAlgebraic. Inference: the basic object of algebraic number theory.

name: Chain complex
def: A sequence of abelian groups or modules $C_n$ with boundary homomorphisms $\partial_n:C_n\to C_{n-1}$ satisfying $\partial_{n-1}\circ\partial_n=0$.
why: 4 catalog results name it (e.g. Dold-Kan correspondence, Eilenberg–Zilber theorem); nLab page 'chain complex' has 252 backlinks; Mathlib defines it as ChainComplex. Inference: the basic object of homological algebra.

name: Conditional probability
def: The probability $P(A\mid B)=P(A\cap B)/P(B)$ of an event $A$ given that an event $B$ of positive probability occurs.
why: 5 catalog results name it (e.g. Bayes rule, Bayes' theorem); Mathlib defines it as ProbabilityTheory.cond. Inference: basic to statistics, Bayesian inference and machine learning.

name: Direct sum
def: The combination $V\oplus W$ of modules or vector spaces as pairs with componentwise operations; for infinitely many summands, families with finitely many nonzero entries.
why: 4 catalog results name it (e.g. Maschke's theorem, Splitting lemma); nLab page 'direct sum' has 316 backlinks; Mathlib defines it as DirectSum. Inference: a basic construction of linear algebra and representation theory.

name: Distribution (generalized function)
def: A continuous linear functional on a space of smooth compactly supported test functions, generalizing functions so that every one is differentiable, as with the Dirac delta.
why: 7 catalog results name it (e.g. Edge-of-the-wedge theorem, Frobenius theorem); nLab page 'distribution' has 73 backlinks. Inference: the setting of linear PDE theory and physics; bare 'distribution' is excluded because it usually means a probability distribution.

name: Euler characteristic
def: The integer $V-E+F$ of a polyhedron, in general the alternating sum of the ranks of the homology groups of a space.
why: 7 catalog results name it (e.g. Gauss–Bonnet theorem, Generalized Gauss-Bonnet theorem); nLab page 'Euler characteristic' has 59 backlinks. Inference: a classical invariant across topology, combinatorics and geometry.

name: Exponential function
def: The function $\exp(x)=e^x=\sum_{n\ge0}x^n/n!$, the unique differentiable function equal to its own derivative with value 1 at 0.
why: 8 catalog results name it (e.g. Chernoff bound, Euler's formula); Mathlib defines it as Real.exp. Inference: ubiquitous in analysis, growth models, physics and finance.

name: Finite field
def: A field with finitely many elements; its size is a prime power $p^n$ and it is unique up to isomorphism, written $\mathbb{F}_{p^n}$.
why: 8 catalog results name it (e.g. Ax–Grothendieck theorem, Brauer–Suzuki–Wall theorem); nLab page 'finite field' has 49 backlinks; Mathlib defines it as GaloisField. Inference: central to number theory, coding theory and cryptography.

name: Free group
def: The group of reduced words in a set of generators and their inverses, multiplied by concatenation and cancellation, satisfying no relations beyond the group axioms.
why: 5 catalog results name it (e.g. Banach–Tarski paradox, Banch-Tarski theorem); nLab page 'free group' has 50 backlinks; Mathlib defines it as FreeGroup. Inference: a basic object of combinatorial and geometric group theory.

name: Haar measure
def: A nonzero left-invariant Radon measure on a locally compact group, unique up to a positive scalar factor.
why: 8 catalog results name it (e.g. Blichfeldt's Theorem, Bochner linearization theorem); Mathlib defines it as MeasureTheory.Measure.haarMeasure. Inference: the basis of harmonic analysis on groups, used in random matrix theory and quantum information.

name: Ideal
def: An additive subgroup $I$ of a ring $R$ that absorbs multiplication, so $ra$ and $ar$ lie in $I$ for all $r\in R$, $a\in I$.
why: Seven catalog results (Chinese remainder theorem, Hilbert basis theorem, Krull) name it and nLab has a page with 140 backlinks; ideals organize all of ring theory and algebraic geometry. Patterns avoid the bare word, which is common in English.

name: Independence (probability)
def: Events or random variables are independent when their joint probabilities factor as the product of the individual probabilities.
why: Nine results (laws of large numbers, Hoeffding, Kolmogorov 0-1 law) rest on it and Mathlib defines iIndepSet; independence is basic to all of statistics and information theory (inference).

name: Lattice (order theory)
def: A partially ordered set in which every pair of elements has a least upper bound (join) and a greatest lower bound (meet).
why: nLab and Mathlib (Lattice) define it. Inference: the order-theoretic notion organizes order theory and appears in logic and program semantics.

name: Lattice (discrete subgroup)
def: A discrete subgroup of $\mathbb{R}^n$ that spans it, equivalently the integer combinations of a basis; more generally a discrete subgroup of finite covolume in a Lie group.
why: The catalog results that name a lattice (Blichfeldt's theorem, the Kepler conjecture, the crystallographic restriction theorem) use this sense. Inference: lattices organize the geometry of numbers, sphere packing and crystallography, and lattice-based cryptography gives practical use.

name: Logarithm
def: The inverse of the exponential function: $\log x$ is the number $y$ with $e^y=x$ for $x>0$, and similarly for other bases.
why: Five catalog results (Baker's theorem, Robbins bound) and Mathlib Real.log with 186 files; logarithms are ubiquitous in science, information theory and complexity.

name: Modular form
def: A holomorphic function on the upper half-plane that transforms by a fixed weight factor under a congruence subgroup of $SL_2(\mathbb Z)$ and is holomorphic at the cusps.
why: Eight results including Fermat's Last Theorem and Jacobi's four-square theorem name it, with an nLab page; a central research object of number theory with string-theory uses but little applied impact.

name: Module
def: An abelian group with a scalar multiplication by elements of a ring that distributes over addition and is associative, generalizing a vector space.
why: Mathlib's Module class is used in 1856 files and nLab defines it; four results (Nakayama, Mitchell embedding) name it and it organizes commutative algebra and representation theory.

name: Monoidal category
def: A category with a tensor product functor and a unit object, associative and unital up to coherent natural isomorphisms.
why: Mathlib (206 files) and nLab define it and four results name it; it organizes quantum algebra and is used in categorical quantum mechanics.

name: Monotone function
def: A function between ordered sets that preserves (or reverses) order: $x\le y$ implies $f(x)\le f(y)$.
why: Eight results (Froda, Fubini differentiation theorem) name it and nLab defines it; elementary and widespread in analysis, economics and optimization.

name: Prime ideal
def: A proper ideal $P$ of a commutative ring such that $ab\in P$ implies $a\in P$ or $b\in P$.
why: Mathlib Ideal.IsPrime (165 files), nLab and five results (going up/down, Eisenstein) name it; basic to commutative algebra and the points of spectra.

name: Projective plane
def: A geometry of points and lines in which any two points lie on exactly one line and any two lines meet in exactly one point, such as the real projective plane.
why: Eight results (Bruck-Ryser-Chowla, Bezout, De Bruijn-Erdos) and an nLab page; important in combinatorial design, coding theory and computer graphics.

name: Self-adjoint operator
def: A linear operator $A$ on a Hilbert space equal to its adjoint, so $\langle Ax,y\rangle=\langle x,Ay\rangle$ on its domain.
why: Nine results (spectral theorem, Cauchy interlacing, Hilbert-Schmidt) and Mathlib IsSelfAdjoint; observables in quantum mechanics are self-adjoint operators.

name: Solvable group
def: A group with a finite chain of subgroups, each normal in the next, whose successive quotients are abelian.
why: Eight results (Abel-Ruffini, Borel fixed-point) and nLab; central to group theory and Galois theory, with few applied uses.

name: Stopping time
def: A random time $\tau$ such that the event $\{\tau\le t\}$ is determined by the information available up to time $t$.
why: Mathlib IsStoppingTime and five results (Doob inequalities, optional sampling); used in finance (American options) and sequential statistics.

name: Sumset
def: For subsets $A,B$ of an abelian group, the set $A+B=\{a+b: a\in A, b\in B\}$ of all pairwise sums.
why: Eight results (Cauchy-Davenport, Freiman, Kneser) name it; it organizes additive combinatorics, with Minkowski sums used in computational geometry. No source record in the packet.

name: Turing machine
def: An abstract machine that reads and writes symbols on an unbounded tape according to a finite table of state transitions, modelling algorithmic computation.
why: Five results (Cook-Levin, halting theorem) and Mathlib Turing.TM0.Machine with nLab; the foundation of computability and complexity theory in computer science.

name: Vector field
def: An assignment of a tangent vector to each point of a manifold or region of space, smoothly varying in the smooth case.
why: Seven results (Lie-Palais, orbit theorem) and nLab; vector fields describe flows and forces throughout physics and engineering.

name: Adjoint functor
def: A pair of functors $F:C\to D$, $G:D\to C$ with a natural bijection $\mathrm{Hom}_D(FX,Y)\cong\mathrm{Hom}_C(X,GY)$.
why: Nine results (Frobenius reciprocity, Isbell duality) and Mathlib Adjunction (197 files) with nLab; adjunctions unify free constructions across mathematics and appear in programming-language semantics.

name: Basis
def: A linearly independent family of vectors that spans a vector space or module, so every element is a unique finite linear combination of them.
why: Mathlib Module.Basis (296 files), nLab and three results (dimension theorem, change of basis); fundamental to linear algebra and all its applications.

name: Bilinear form
def: A map $B:V\times V\to K$ on a vector space that is linear in each argument separately.
why: Six results (Lax-Milgram, Grothendieck inequality) and nLab; used in finite-element methods and physics.

name: Convolution
def: The function $(f*g)(x)=\int f(y)g(x-y)\,dy$ (or a sum in the discrete case) obtained by averaging one function against translates of another.
why: Mathlib MeasureTheory.convolution and four results (convolution theorem, Titchmarsh); central in signal processing, probability and convolutional neural networks, so the word also names ML layers.

name: CW complex
def: A topological space built inductively by attaching cells of increasing dimension along their boundaries.
why: Seven results (Hurewicz, Brown representability, Hopf degree) and nLab; the standard spaces of homotopy theory.

name: Divisor (algebraic geometry)
def: A formal integer combination of codimension-one subvarieties of a variety, such as the zeros and poles of a rational function.
why: Seven results (Clifford special divisors, Abel-Jacobi) and nLab; basic to algebraic geometry, applied only through algebraic coding.

name: Elementary embedding
def: A map between structures of the same language that preserves the truth of every first-order formula with parameters.
why: Mathlib FirstOrder.Language.ElementaryEmbedding and four results (Tarski-Vaught, Kunen inconsistency); central to model theory and large cardinals only.

name: Entire function
def: A function holomorphic on the whole complex plane.
why: Seven results (Liouville, Carlson, Akhiezer) and nLab; a core class of complex analysis.

name: Exponential map
def: The map sending a tangent vector $v$ to the point reached at time one along the geodesic, or one-parameter subgroup, with initial velocity $v$.
why: Seven results (Cartan closed subgroup, Cartan-Hadamard) and nLab; used in robotics and optimization on manifolds.

name: Filter (order theory)
def: A nonempty upward-closed family of subsets (or poset elements) closed under finite intersections (meets) and not containing the empty set.
why: Mathlib Filter (1290 files) and nLab, with three results (Tychonoff, ultrafilter theorem); filters unify limits in topology and logic. The bare word is excluded as ambiguous.

name: Greatest common divisor
def: The largest integer (or a maximal common divisor in a ring) dividing each of the given elements.
why: Seven results (Bezout identity, Chinese remainder theorem) and nLab; gcd computation is basic to cryptography and computer algebra.

name: Homotopy group
def: The group $\pi_n(X,x)$ of homotopy classes of based maps from the $n$-sphere into a space $X$.
why: Six results (Freudenthal, Bott periodicity) and nLab; central invariant in algebraic topology with physics uses for defects.

name: Hopf algebra
def: A bialgebra with an antipode map satisfying the axiom that makes it behave like functions on a group.
why: Six results (Milnor-Moore, Cartier duality) and nLab; organizes quantum groups and combinatorial algebra, with renormalization uses in physics.

name: Topological K-theory
def: The generalized cohomology theory whose groups $K(X)$ are built from isomorphism classes of vector bundles over a space by group completion.
why: Six results (Atiyah-Singer, Adams conjecture) and nLab; central to index theory with string-theory and topological-phase uses.

name: Lie bracket
def: The bilinear antisymmetric operation of a Lie algebra satisfying the Jacobi identity, such as the commutator $[X,Y]=XY-YX$ of vector fields.
why: Seven results (Frobenius theorem, Jacobi identity) name it; used in control theory and mechanics. No source record in the packet.

name: Line bundle
def: A vector bundle whose fibres are one-dimensional.
why: Six results (Borel-Weil, Appell-Humbert) and nLab; central in algebraic geometry with gauge-theory uses.

name: Linear map
def: A function between vector spaces or modules that preserves addition and scalar multiplication.
why: Mathlib LinearMap (960 files), nLab and three results (rank-nullity, closed graph); linear maps underpin all of applied linear algebra.

name: Localization of a ring
def: The ring $S^{-1}R$ of fractions $r/s$ obtained from a commutative ring by formally inverting a multiplicative subset $S$.
why: Mathlib Localization (321 files), nLab and three results; a basic tool of commutative algebra and algebraic geometry.

name: Normal distribution
def: The continuous probability distribution with density proportional to $e^{-(x-\mu)^2/(2\sigma^2)}$, determined by its mean and variance.
why: Seven results (Berry-Esseen, Cochran, Cramer) name it; the most used distribution in science and statistics. Mathlib defines ProbabilityTheory.gaussianReal.

name: Probability measure
def: A measure on a sigma-algebra that assigns total mass one to the whole space.
why: Mathlib IsProbabilityMeasure, nLab (probability space) and four results (Jensen, union bound); the foundation of probability theory and statistics.

name: Quotient group
def: The group $G/N$ of cosets of a normal subgroup $N$ in $G$, with multiplication $(aN)(bN)=abN$.
why: Six results (Goursat lemma, Vitali set) and nLab; a basic group-theory construction.

name: Regular language
def: A formal language recognised by a finite automaton, equivalently described by a regular expression.
why: Mathlib Language.IsRegular, nLab and four results (Arden, Buchi-Elgot-Trakhtenbrot); basic to compilers, text search and verification.

name: Sectional curvature
def: The Gaussian curvature of the surface swept out by geodesics tangent to a given 2-plane in the tangent space of a Riemannian manifold.
why: Seven results (Cartan-Hadamard, Rauch comparison, Synge) and nLab; central to comparison geometry.

name: Set
def: A collection of distinct objects, its elements, determined entirely by which objects it contains.
why: Mathlib Set (3825 files), nLab and three results (Cantor, Russell paradox); the base notion of almost all mathematics. Patterns avoid the everyday word.

name: Simple group
def: A nontrivial group whose only normal subgroups are the trivial group and itself.
why: Mathlib IsSimpleGroup, nLab and four results including the classification of finite simple groups; the building blocks of finite groups.

name: Smooth function
def: A function with continuous derivatives of every order.
why: Seven results (Borel, Hadamard lemma, Malgrange preparation) name it; used across analysis, geometry and applied modelling. Mathlib ContDiff with infinite order defines it.

name: Sphere
def: The set of points at a fixed distance from a centre point, such as the $n$-sphere $S^n$ in $\mathbb R^{n+1}$.
why: Six results (Borsuk-Ulam, Alexander duality) and nLab; spheres appear everywhere in topology, geometry and physics.

name: Variance
def: The expected squared deviation of a random variable from its mean, $\mathrm{Var}(X)=E[(X-EX)^2]$.
why: Seven results (Chebyshev inequality, Gauss-Markov) name it and Mathlib defines ProbabilityTheory.variance; fundamental in statistics and finance.

name: von Neumann algebra
def: A unital *-algebra of bounded operators on a Hilbert space closed in the weak operator topology, equivalently equal to its double commutant.
why: Six results (Kaplansky density, commutation theorem) and nLab; core of operator algebras with uses in quantum field theory and quantum information.

name: Abelian variety
def: A complete connected algebraic group, equivalently a projective variety with a compatible group law.
why: Six results (Chevalley structure, Katz-Lang finiteness) and nLab; central in arithmetic geometry with cryptographic uses (elliptic and hyperelliptic curves).

name: Arithmetic progression
def: A sequence of numbers in which consecutive terms differ by a fixed constant, $a, a+d, a+2d,\dots$.
why: Six results (Roth, Brun-Titchmarsh, Behrend construction) name it; central to additive combinatorics. No source record in the packet.

name: Category
def: A collection of objects and morphisms between them, with an associative composition of morphisms and identity morphisms.
why: Mathlib Category (1755 files) and nLab; only two catalog results name it but categories unify modern algebra and topology and appear in programming-language theory.
revised: tc-judge-revision/1: phrases narrowed after the first arXiv count showed everyday or other-field senses

name: Clifford algebra
def: The associative algebra generated by a vector space with quadratic form $Q$ subject to $v^2=Q(v)$.
why: Mathlib CliffordAlgebra and nLab, with two results (Fierz identity, Lichnerowicz formula); used for spinors in physics and in geometric algebra for graphics.

name: Closed set
def: A subset of a topological space whose complement is open, equivalently one containing all its limit points.
why: Six results (Heine-Borel, Tietze extension, Cantor intersection) name it; basic topology. Mathlib IsClosed defines it.

name: Cobordism
def: Two closed manifolds are cobordant when together they form the boundary of a compact manifold of one dimension more.
why: Five results (Hirzebruch signature, Pontryagin, s-cobordism) and nLab; central in geometric topology and topological field theory.

name: Compact Hausdorff space
def: A topological space that is both compact and Hausdorff.
why: Five results (Gelfand duality, Stone-Weierstrass) and nLab; the standard setting of functional analysis on spaces.

name: Compact operator
def: A linear operator between Banach spaces that maps bounded sets to relatively compact sets.
why: Six results (Fredholm, Atkinson, analytic Fredholm) and nLab; used in integral equations and numerical analysis.

name: Convex body
def: A compact convex subset of Euclidean space with nonempty interior.
why: Six results (Busemann, Hadwiger, Anderson) name it; core of convex geometry with uses in optimization. Mathlib ConvexBody defines it.

name: Countable set
def: A set that can be put in bijection with a subset of the natural numbers.
why: Five results (Cantor-Bendixson, countability of rationals) and nLab; used across analysis, probability and logic.

name: Curvature
def: A measure of how far a curve, surface or Riemannian manifold deviates from being flat, captured by the Riemann curvature tensor in general.
why: Five results (Bianchi identity, Fenchel, Descartes) and nLab; curvature is central in geometry, general relativity and graphics.

name: Derived category
def: The category obtained from chain complexes over an abelian category by formally inverting quasi-isomorphisms.
why: Five results (Bondal-Orlov, Grothendieck duality, Fourier-Mukai) with nLab and Mathlib DerivedCategory; central in modern algebraic geometry, with string-theory uses (homological mirror symmetry).

name: Differential form
def: A smooth section of an exterior power of the cotangent bundle, an object that can be integrated over oriented submanifolds.
why: Five results (Stokes, Poincare lemma) and nLab; organizes calculus on manifolds and electromagnetism.

name: Distributive lattice
def: A lattice in which meet distributes over join, $a\wedge(b\vee c)=(a\wedge b)\vee(a\wedge c)$.
why: Five results (Birkhoff representation, FKG, Ahlswede-Daykin) and nLab; used in combinatorics and statistical physics correlation inequalities.

name: Dual space
def: The vector space of (continuous) linear functionals on a given vector space.
why: Mathlib StrongDual, nLab and three results (Banach-Alaoglu, Riesz representation); duality appears in optimization and physics.

name: Equilateral triangle
def: A triangle whose three sides have equal length, equivalently whose three angles are each $60^\circ$.
why: Six results (Napoleon, Morley trisector) name it; a narrow elementary object with no source record.

name: Extreme point
def: A point of a convex set that is not an interior point of any line segment contained in the set.
why: Mathlib Set.extremePoints, nLab and three results (Krein-Milman, Choquet theory); basic to linear programming.

name: Functor
def: A map between categories sending objects to objects and morphisms to morphisms while preserving composition and identities.
why: Mathlib Functor (1075 files) and nLab; only two results name it but functors are the basic maps of category theory and appear in functional programming.

name: Fundamental group
def: The group of homotopy classes of loops based at a point of a space, with concatenation of loops as the operation.
why: Five results (Mostow rigidity, Dehn-Nielsen-Baer) and nLab; a central invariant in topology. Mathlib FundamentalGroup defines it.

name: Galois group
def: The group of automorphisms of a field extension that fix the base field pointwise.
why: Five results (Abel-Ruffini, Artin reciprocity) and nLab; central to number theory and algebra.

name: General linear group
def: The group $GL_n(K)$ of invertible $n\times n$ matrices over a field or ring, equivalently the invertible linear maps of a vector space.
why: Mathlib Matrix.GeneralLinearGroup, nLab and two results (Schur-Weyl duality, Kuiper); appears throughout representation theory and physics.

name: Graph coloring
def: An assignment of colors to the vertices of a graph such that adjacent vertices receive different colors.
why: Six results (Brooks theorem, De Bruijn-Erdos) name it and Mathlib defines SimpleGraph.Coloring; used in scheduling and register allocation.

name: Gödel numbering
def: An injective encoding of the symbols, formulas and proofs of a formal language as natural numbers.
why: Six results (incompleteness theorems, Kleene recursion theorem) and nLab; a technical device of logic and computability.

name: Incircle
def: The largest circle contained in a triangle or polygon, tangent to each of its sides.
why: Six results (Feuerbach point, Euler theorem in geometry) name it; a narrow topic of triangle geometry with no source record.

name: Intersection form
def: The symmetric bilinear form on the middle homology (or cohomology) of a closed oriented $4k$-manifold given by counting intersections of cycles.
why: Six results (Donaldson, Freedman classification, Furuta) name it; a key invariant of 4-manifold topology without a packet source.

name: Irreducible polynomial
def: A non-constant polynomial that cannot be written as a product of two non-constant polynomials over the given ring or field.
why: Mathlib Irreducible, nLab and three results (Eisenstein criterion, Hilbert irreducibility); used in coding theory and cryptography.

name: Linear independence
def: A family of vectors is linearly independent when no nontrivial linear combination of them equals zero.
why: Mathlib LinearIndependent (147 files) and three results (Steinitz exchange, six exponentials); basic to linear algebra and its applications.

name: System of linear equations
def: A finite set of linear equations in common unknowns, written $Ax=b$ for a matrix $A$ and vector $b$.
why: Six results (Cramer theorem, Cayley-Bacharach) name it; solving linear systems is the core of numerical computing. No packet source.

name: Lipschitz continuous function
def: A function between metric spaces with a constant $K$ such that $d(f(x),f(y))\le K\,d(x,y)$ for all $x,y$.
why: Mathlib LipschitzWith and three results (Picard-Lindelof, Kantorovich); used widely in ODEs, optimization and machine learning.

name: Matching (graph theory)
def: A set of edges in a graph no two of which share a vertex.
why: Mathlib SimpleGraph.Subgraph.IsMatching and three results (Hall marriage, Konig, Berge); matching algorithms are used in assignment and economics.

name: Maximal ideal
def: A proper ideal of a ring not contained in any strictly larger proper ideal.
why: Mathlib Ideal.IsMaximal (122 files), nLab and three results (Krull, Gelfand duality); basic commutative algebra.

name: Meromorphic function
def: A function on an open subset of the complex plane or a Riemann surface that is holomorphic except at isolated poles.
why: Six results (Jensen formula, canonical decomposition) and nLab; central in complex analysis and number theory. Mathlib MeromorphicAt.

name: Open cover
def: A family of open subsets of a topological space whose union is the whole space.
why: Five results (Heine-Borel, Lebesgue number lemma, Michael) and nLab; basic topological notion.

name: Presheaf
def: A contravariant functor from a category, such as the open sets of a space, to sets or another category.
why: Five results (Barr embedding, Elmendorf, Isbell duality) and nLab; basic in sheaf theory and category theory.

name: Group representation
def: A homomorphism from a group to the group of invertible linear maps of a vector space.
why: Mathlib Representation, nLab and four results (Maschke, Frobenius reciprocity); used in chemistry and particle physics.

name: Family of sets
def: A collection of subsets of a given set, possibly indexed, considered as a single object.
why: Six results (Bondy theorem, Ahlswede-Zhang, Assouad bound) and nLab; the basic object of extremal set theory.

name: Similar triangles
def: Two triangles are similar when their corresponding angles are equal, equivalently when corresponding sides are proportional.
why: Six results (angle bisector theorem, geometric mean theorem) name it; school geometry used in surveying. No source record.

name: Simplicial object
def: A contravariant functor from the simplex category to a category, giving objects in each dimension with face and degeneracy maps.
why: Five results (bar construction, Waldhausen S-construction) and nLab; central in homotopy theory. Mathlib CategoryTheory.SimplicialObject.

name: Smooth manifold
def: A topological manifold with an atlas of charts whose transition maps are infinitely differentiable.
why: Five results (Whitney embedding) and nLab; the setting of differential geometry, physics and robotics.

name: Trace of a matrix
def: The sum of the diagonal entries of a square matrix, equal to the sum of its eigenvalues.
why: Five results (Lefschetz trace formula, crystallographic restriction) and nLab; ubiquitous in physics and statistics. Mathlib Matrix.trace.

name: Uniform integrability
def: A family of integrable functions whose integrals over sets where they are large tend to zero uniformly over the family.
why: Mathlib MeasureTheory.UniformIntegrable and three results (Vitali convergence, martingale convergence); a technical tool of probability.

name: Unitary representation
def: A homomorphism from a group into the unitary operators of a Hilbert space, usually continuous in the strong topology.
why: Six results (Kirillov correspondence, Haag theorem, Gelfand-Raikov) and nLab; underlies quantum mechanics symmetries.

name: VC dimension
def: The largest size of a set that a family of sets shatters, that is, whose every subset is cut out by some member of the family.
why: Mathlib Finset.vcDim and three results (Sauer-Shelah, Assouad bound); a key notion in learning theory.

name: Vector bundle
def: A continuous family of vector spaces parametrized by a base space, locally isomorphic to a product of the base with a fixed vector space.
why: Five results (Serre-Swan, Hirzebruch-Riemann-Roch, Harder-Narasimhan) and nLab; central in geometry and gauge theory. Mathlib VectorBundle.

name: Algebraic K-theory
def: A sequence of functors $K_n$ assigning abelian groups to a ring or category, starting from the Grothendieck group of projective modules.
why: Four results (Quillen Q-construction, Lichtenbaum-Quillen) and nLab; a deep research subject with no applied use.

name: Almost sure convergence
def: A sequence of random variables converges almost surely when it converges pointwise outside an event of probability zero.
why: Five results (strong law of large numbers, Egorov, Skorokhod) name it; the packet's Mathlib record is the a.e. filter, not the convergence notion.

name: Alternating group
def: The subgroup $A_n$ of the symmetric group $S_n$ consisting of the even permutations, those that are products of an even number of transpositions.
why: 2 catalog results name it (Jordan's theorem, alternating groups on 5 letters or more are simple); defined in Mathlib `alternatingGroup` and nLab 'alternating group'. Inference: a basic family of finite simple groups, central to finite group theory but with modest applied use.

name: Analytic set
def: A subset of a complex manifold that is locally the common zero set of finitely many holomorphic functions.
why: 5 catalog results name it (Chow's theorem, Lusin separation theorem); no mathlib or nLab record. Inference: the packet merges the complex-analytic sense (Chow, Remmert-Stein, Siu) with the descriptive-set-theory Suslin sense (Lusin, Suslin), so pattern counts mix two concepts.

name: Ball (metric space)
def: The set of points of a metric space whose distance from a centre $x$ is less than (open ball) or at most (closed ball) a radius $r$.
why: 2 catalog results name it (Alexander's trick, Vitali covering lemma); defined in Mathlib `Metric.ball` and nLab 'ball'. Inference: a basic building block of analysis and geometry used wherever distances appear.

name: Brownian motion
def: A stochastic process $B_t$ with $B_0=0$, continuous paths and independent increments $B_t-B_s$ that are normally distributed with mean 0 and variance $t-s$.
why: 5 catalog results name it (Donsker's theorem, Feynman-Kac formula); defined in nLab 'Brownian motion'. Inference: the core continuous-time process of stochastic analysis with heavy use in physics and finance.

name: Characteristic polynomial
def: For a square matrix $A$, the polynomial $\det(tI-A)$, whose roots are the eigenvalues of $A$.
why: 2 catalog results name it (Cayley–Hamilton theorem, existence of an eigenvalue); defined in Mathlib `Matrix.charpoly` and nLab 'characteristic polynomial'. Inference: a standard linear-algebra invariant computed directly from a determinant.

name: Coequalizer
def: The colimit of a pair of parallel morphisms $f,g:A\to B$: a morphism $q:B\to Q$ with $qf=qg$ through which every such morphism factors uniquely.
why: 4 catalog results name it (Beck's monadicity theorem, adjoint lifting theorem); defined in Mathlib `CategoryTheory.Limits.coequalizer` and nLab 'coequalizer'. Inference: a basic colimit shape used in monadicity and adjoint-lifting results.

name: Cohomology
def: A sequence of abelian groups $H^n$ attached contravariantly to a space or algebraic object, computed from a cochain complex and dual to homology.
why: 4 catalog results name it (Poincaré duality, hyperplane section theorem); defined in nLab 'cohomology'. Inference: a central organizing invariant across topology, geometry and number theory.

name: Compact group
def: A topological group whose underlying topological space is compact Hausdorff.
why: 5 catalog results name it (Doplicher-Roberts reconstruction theorem, Gabriel-Oberst duality); no mathlib or nLab record. Inference: Haar measure and Peter-Weyl make it the natural setting for harmonic analysis on groups.

name: Complete metric space
def: A metric space in which every Cauchy sequence converges to a point of the space.
why: 5 catalog results name it (Baire category theorem, Banach fixed-point theorem); defined in Mathlib `CompleteSpace`. Inference: the hypothesis behind Baire and Banach fixed-point arguments throughout analysis.

name: Computable function
def: A function on natural numbers whose values can be calculated by an algorithm, formally by a Turing machine that halts with the output on every input.
why: 8 catalog results name it (Blum's speedup theorem, Compression theorem); defined in Mathlib `Computable` and nLab 'computable function'. Inference: the foundational notion of computability theory, with direct bearing on computer science.

name: Conic section
def: A plane curve cut from a double cone by a plane, an ellipse, parabola or hyperbola, equivalently the zero set of a degree-two polynomial in two variables.
why: 5 catalog results name it (Brianchon's theorem, Dandelin spheres); defined in nLab 'conic section'. Inference: classical projective and Euclidean geometry with uses in optics and orbital mechanics.

name: Convergence in distribution
def: Random variables $X_n$ converge in distribution to $X$ when their distribution functions converge to that of $X$ at every continuity point.
why: 5 catalog results name it (Continuous Mapping Theorem, Cramér–Wold theorem); no mathlib or nLab record. Inference: the mode of convergence in limit theorems such as the central limit theorem, heavily used in statistics.

name: Convex cone
def: A subset of a real vector space closed under addition and under multiplication by positive scalars.
why: 2 catalog results name it (Farkas' lemma, M. Riesz extension theorem); defined in Mathlib `ConvexCone` and nLab 'convex cone'. Inference: the geometric setting of duality and conic optimization.

name: Covering space
def: A continuous surjection $p:E\to X$ such that every point of $X$ has an open neighbourhood whose preimage is a disjoint union of open sets each mapped homeomorphically onto it.
why: 4 catalog results name it (Kurosh subgroup theorem, Nielsen–Schreier theorem); defined in Mathlib `IsCoveringMap` and nLab 'covering space'. Inference: ties the fundamental group to subgroup theory (Nielsen-Schreier, Kurosh) and Riemann surfaces.

name: Cross product
def: The binary operation on $\mathbb{R}^3$ giving a vector perpendicular to both factors whose length is the area of the parallelogram they span.
why: 2 catalog results name it (Jacobi identity, triple product); defined in Mathlib `crossProduct` and nLab 'cross product'. Inference: a narrow three-dimensional construction with very wide use in physics and engineering.

name: Cyclic quadrilateral
def: A quadrilateral whose four vertices lie on a single circle.
why: 5 catalog results name it (Brahmagupta theorem, Japanese theorem for cyclic quadrilaterals); no mathlib or nLab record. Inference: a topic of elementary Euclidean geometry with little research or applied use.

name: Cyclotomic field
def: The number field $\mathbb{Q}(\zeta_n)$ obtained by adjoining a primitive $n$-th root of unity to the rationals.
why: 5 catalog results name it (Catalan's conjecture, Ferrero–Washington theorem); defined in Mathlib `CyclotomicField` and nLab 'cyclotomic field'. Inference: the main test case of algebraic number theory, from Kummer's work on Fermat to Iwasawa theory.

name: D-module
def: A module over the sheaf of differential operators on a smooth algebraic variety or complex manifold, encoding systems of linear partial differential equations.
why: 4 catalog results name it (Riemann-Hilbert correspondence, categorical geometric Langlands conjecture); defined in nLab 'D-module'. Inference: underlies the Riemann-Hilbert correspondence and geometric Langlands.

name: Discriminant
def: An invariant, such as the product of squared differences of a polynomial's roots or the determinant of the trace form of a number field, whose vanishing or size detects repeated roots or ramification.
why: 5 catalog results name it (Brauer–Siegel theorem, Hermite Theorem); defined in nLab 'discriminant'. Inference: used for polynomials, quadratic forms and number fields (Hermite-Minkowski, Brauer-Siegel).

name: Divisibility
def: An integer $a$ divides an integer $b$ when $b=ak$ for some integer $k$; more generally the same relation in any commutative ring.
why: 5 catalog results name it (Euclid's theorem, Lifting the exponent lemma); defined in Mathlib `Dvd`. Inference: the basic relation of elementary number theory behind unique factorization and modular arithmetic.

name: Eigenvector
def: A nonzero vector $v$ that a linear map $A$ sends to a scalar multiple of itself, $Av=\lambda v$.
why: 2 catalog results name it (diagonalization of self-adjoint endomorphisms, eigendecomposition of a matrix); defined in Mathlib `Module.End.HasEigenvector` and nLab 'eigenvector'. Inference: central in linear algebra with wide use in physics, statistics (PCA) and network ranking.

name: Field
def: A commutative ring in which $0\ne1$ and every nonzero element has a multiplicative inverse.
why: 1 catalog result name it (Lagrange's theorem); defined in Mathlib `Field` and nLab 'field'. Inference: a top-level algebraic structure that underlies linear algebra, number theory and coding.

name: Fixed point
def: A point $x$ that a map $f$ sends to itself, $f(x)=x$.
why: 4 catalog results name it (Atiyah-Bott fixed point formula, Burnside's lemma); defined in Mathlib `Function.IsFixedPt` and nLab 'fixed point'. Inference: fixed-point theorems organize results across topology, analysis, dynamics, economics and computing.

name: Foliation
def: A decomposition of a manifold into disjoint connected immersed submanifolds of a fixed dimension, the leaves, that locally look like parallel slices of $\mathbb{R}^n$.
why: 5 catalog results name it (Frobenius theorem, Haefliger theorem); defined in nLab 'foliation'. Inference: a research-level structure in geometric topology and dynamics.

name: Fourier series
def: The expansion of a periodic function as a sum of sines and cosines, or of exponentials $e^{inx}$, whose coefficients are integrals of the function against them.
why: 5 catalog results name it (Basel problem, Parseval's theorem); no mathlib or nLab record. Inference: a pillar of harmonic analysis with pervasive use in signal processing and physics.

name: Galois representation
def: A continuous homomorphism from the absolute Galois group of a field to $GL_n$ of a topological field or ring such as $\mathbb{Q}_\ell$ or $\mathbb{F}_p$.
why: 5 catalog results name it (Fermat's Last Theorem, Ribet's theorem); defined in nLab 'Galois representation'. Inference: central to modern number theory, from Fermat's Last Theorem to the Langlands programme.

name: Gaussian measure
def: A Borel probability measure on $\mathbb{R}^n$ or a locally convex space all of whose one-dimensional linear images are normal distributions.
why: 5 catalog results name it (Bargmann-Segal transform, Cameron–Martin theorem); defined in nLab 'Gaussian measure'. Inference: the infinite-dimensional setting of Cameron-Martin and Fernique with uses in statistics and quantum field theory.

name: Generating function
def: A formal power series $\sum a_n x^n$ (or a variant) whose coefficients encode a sequence $a_n$, so that operations on series express facts about the sequence.
why: 5 catalog results name it (Chomsky–Schützenberger enumeration theorem, Glaisher's theorem); defined in nLab 'generating function'. Inference: the main counting tool of enumerative combinatorics, also used in probability and physics.

name: Geodesic
def: A curve in a Riemannian (or affinely connected) manifold that locally minimizes length, equivalently has zero covariant acceleration.
why: 5 catalog results name it (Beltrami's theorem, Gauss–Bonnet theorem); defined in nLab 'geodesic'. Inference: organizes Riemannian geometry and general relativity and appears in metric geometry.

name: Hardy space
def: The space $H^p$ of holomorphic functions on the unit disc (or a half-plane) whose $L^p$ means over circles of radius $r$ stay bounded as $r\to1$.
why: 5 catalog results name it (Beurling–Lax theorem, Carleson–Jacobs theorem); no mathlib or nLab record. Inference: a central space of operator theory and complex analysis with uses in control and signal theory.

name: Harmonic function
def: A twice continuously differentiable real function on an open subset of $\mathbb{R}^n$ whose Laplacian $\sum \partial^2 f/\partial x_i^2$ vanishes.
why: 5 catalog results name it (Bôcher's theorem, Harnack's principle); defined in nLab 'harmonic function'. Inference: solutions of Laplace's equation, central to potential theory and physics.

name: Homotopy equivalence
def: A continuous map $f:X\to Y$ with a continuous $g:Y\to X$ such that $g\circ f$ and $f\circ g$ are homotopic to the identities.
why: 4 catalog results name it (Dowker duality, Dowker's theorem); defined in Mathlib `ContinuousMap.HomotopyEquiv` and nLab 'homotopy equivalence'. Inference: the basic notion of sameness in homotopy theory.

name: Induced representation
def: A representation of a group $G$ built from a representation $V$ of a subgroup $H$, for finite groups $k[G]\otimes_{k[H]}V$.
why: 5 catalog results name it (Artin induction theorem, Brauer's theorem on induced characters); defined in nLab 'induced representation'. Inference: the main construction of representations, behind Frobenius reciprocity and Brauer's theorem.

name: Isomorphism
def: A structure-preserving map with a structure-preserving two-sided inverse; in a category, a morphism with a two-sided inverse.
why: 1 catalog result name it (structure identity principle); defined in Mathlib `CategoryTheory.Iso` and nLab 'isomorphism'. Inference: the universal notion of sameness of structures across mathematics.

name: Locally convex space
def: A topological vector space whose topology has a base of convex neighbourhoods of zero, equivalently one defined by a family of seminorms.
why: 5 catalog results name it (Krein-Milman lemma, Krein–Milman theorem); defined in Mathlib `LocallyConvexSpace` and nLab 'locally convex topological vector space'. Inference: the general setting of Hahn-Banach and Krein-Milman and of distribution theory.

name: Manifold
def: A Hausdorff, second-countable topological space in which every point has a neighbourhood homeomorphic to an open subset of $\mathbb{R}^n$.
why: 4 catalog results name it (Poincaré–Hopf theorem, discrete spaces are 0-manifolds); defined in nLab 'manifold'. Inference: a top-level organizing notion of geometry and topology also used in physics and machine learning.

name: Mapping class group
def: The group of isotopy classes of orientation-preserving homeomorphisms of a surface or manifold.
why: 5 catalog results name it (Dehn twist, Dehn-Nielsen-Baer theorem); defined in nLab 'mapping class group'. Inference: a major object of low-dimensional topology and geometric group theory.

name: Measurable function
def: A function between measurable spaces under which the preimage of every measurable set is measurable.
why: 2 catalog results name it (Lusin's theorem, approximation by step functions); defined in Mathlib `Measurable` and nLab 'measurable function'. Inference: the functions integration and probability are built on, random variables being one case.

name: Minimal polynomial
def: The monic polynomial of least degree over a field that has a given algebraic element or a given square matrix as a root.
why: 2 catalog results name it (Joubert's theorem, Kummer-Dedekind Theorem); defined in Mathlib `minpoly`. Inference: a standard invariant of field extensions and linear maps.

name: Natural transformation
def: A family of morphisms $\eta_X:F(X)\to G(X)$ between two functors $F,G$, one for each object $X$, commuting with the images of every morphism.
why: 1 catalog result name it (Yoneda lemma); defined in Mathlib `CategoryTheory.NatTrans` and nLab 'natural transformation'. Inference: one of the three founding notions of category theory.

name: Nilpotent group
def: A group whose lower central series reaches the trivial subgroup after finitely many steps.
why: 2 catalog results name it (Fitting's theorem, Gromov's theorem on groups of polynomial growth); defined in Mathlib `Group.IsNilpotent` and nLab 'nilpotent group'. Inference: a structural class of groups behind Gromov's polynomial growth theorem.

name: Normed space
def: A real or complex vector space equipped with a norm.
why: 5 catalog results name it (Fréchet–von Neumann–Jordan Theorem, Hahn–Banach theorem); defined in Mathlib `NormedSpace` and nLab 'normed vector space'. Inference: the basic setting of functional analysis (Hahn-Banach, Mazur-Ulam).

name: Ordered ring
def: A ring with a total order such that $a\le b$ implies $a+c\le b+c$, and $0\le a,0\le b$ imply $0\le ab$.
why: 2 catalog results name it (Bernoulli's inequality, arithmetic mean-geometric mean inequality); defined in Mathlib `IsOrderedRing` and nLab 'ordered ring'. Inference: the abstract setting of inequalities in the integers and reals.

name: Orthogonal group
def: The group $O(n)$ of $n\times n$ real matrices $Q$ with $Q^TQ=I$, the linear isometries of Euclidean space; more generally the isometries of a quadratic form.
why: 1 catalog result name it (Witt's theorem); defined in Mathlib `Matrix.orthogonalGroup` and nLab 'orthogonal group'. Inference: a classical group with uses in physics, mechanics and numerical linear algebra.

name: Partial order
def: A binary relation that is reflexive, antisymmetric and transitive.
why: 4 catalog results name it (Hausdorff maximal principle, Hausdorff's maximality principle); defined in Mathlib `PartialOrder` and nLab 'partial order'. Inference: an elementary structure organizing order theory, lattice theory and computer-science semantics.

name: Peano arithmetic
def: The first-order theory of the natural numbers with zero, successor, addition and multiplication axioms and the induction schema.
why: 5 catalog results name it (Kanamori–McAloon theorem, Kirby–Paris theorem); defined in nLab 'Peano arithmetic'. Inference: the base theory for incompleteness and independence results (Paris-Harrington, Kirby-Paris).

name: Polynomial ring
def: The ring $R[x_1,\dots,x_n]$ of polynomials in the variables $x_i$ with coefficients in a ring $R$.
why: 8 catalog results name it (Chevalley–Warning theorem, Hilbert's Nullstellensatz); defined in Mathlib `Polynomial`. Inference: the basic ring of commutative algebra and algebraic geometry (Nullstellensatz, basis theorem), eight results.

name: Principal bundle
def: A fibre bundle $P\to X$ with a continuous right action of a group $G$ that is free and transitive on each fibre and locally trivial.
why: 4 catalog results name it (Milnor construction, Weil uniformization theorem); defined in nLab 'principal bundle'. Inference: the geometric language of gauge theory and classifying spaces.

why: 5 catalog results name it (Fubini's theorem, Ionescu-Tulcea theorem); defined in Mathlib `MeasureTheory.Measure.prod`. Inference: the setting of Fubini's theorem and of independent random variables.

name: Projective module
def: A module that is a direct summand of a free module, equivalently one for which every surjection onto it splits.
why: 4 catalog results name it (Quillen–Suslin theorem, Schanuel's lemma); defined in Mathlib `Module.Projective` and nLab 'projective module'. Inference: central to homological algebra and algebraic K-theory (Quillen-Suslin, Serre-Swan).

name: Quotient space
def: The set of equivalence classes of a topological space under an equivalence relation, with the finest topology making the projection map continuous.
why: 1 catalog result name it (Arnold-Kuiper-Massey theorem); defined in nLab 'quotient space'. Inference: a basic construction of topology (gluing, orbit spaces); the phrase also names linear quotient spaces.

name: Radius of convergence
def: The supremum of the $r\ge0$ for which a power series $\sum a_n(z-c)^n$ converges whenever $|z-c|<r$.
why: 2 catalog results name it (Cauchy–Hadamard theorem, differentiability with respect to the complex variable); defined in Mathlib `FormalMultilinearSeries.radius`. Inference: a standard invariant of power series computed by Cauchy-Hadamard.

name: Radon measure
def: A Borel measure on a Hausdorff space that is finite on compact sets and inner regular, approximating open sets from inside by compact sets.
why: 5 catalog results name it (Besicovitch covering theorem, Disintegration theorem); defined in nLab 'Radon measure'. Inference: the measures of the Riesz representation theorem, used in geometric measure theory.

name: Real number
def: An element of the complete ordered field $\mathbb{R}$, constructible from the rationals by Cauchy sequences or Dedekind cuts.
why: 1 catalog result name it (Dirichlet's approximation theorem); defined in Mathlib `Real` and nLab 'real number'. Inference: the number system underlying analysis and every quantitative application.

name: Reductive group
def: A linear algebraic group over a field whose unipotent radical (over an algebraic closure) is trivial, such as $GL_n$, $SL_n$ or $Sp_{2n}$.
why: 5 catalog results name it (Arthur-Selberg trace formula, Bruhat decomposition); defined in nLab 'reductive group'. Inference: the groups of the Langlands programme and the trace formula.

name: Ring
def: A set with an addition making it an abelian group and an associative multiplication with identity that distributes over addition.
why: 1 catalog result name it (Jacobson's lemma); defined in Mathlib `Ring` and nLab 'ring'. Inference: a top-level algebraic structure across algebra, number theory and geometry.

name: Semisimple Lie group
def: A connected Lie group whose Lie algebra is semisimple, that is, has no nonzero solvable ideals.
why: 5 catalog results name it (Harish-Chandra's regularity theorem, Iwasawa decomposition); defined in nLab 'semisimple Lie group'. Inference: the main class of Harish-Chandra's harmonic analysis and of symmetric spaces.

name: Simplicial complex
def: A collection of simplices closed under taking faces in which any two simplices meet in a common face, or abstractly a downward-closed family of finite sets.
why: 5 catalog results name it (Dowker duality, Kruskal–Katona theorem); defined in Mathlib `Geometry.SimplicialComplex` and nLab 'simplicial complex'. Inference: combinatorial models of spaces used in topology, combinatorics and topological data analysis.

name: Sobolev space
def: The space $W^{k,p}$ of $L^p$ functions whose weak derivatives up to order $k$ also lie in $L^p$.
why: 5 catalog results name it (Gagliardo-Nirenberg-Sobolev inequality, Quasiconformal mapping); defined in nLab 'Sobolev space'. Inference: the function spaces of PDE theory and finite element analysis.

name: Stein manifold
def: A complex manifold that is holomorphically convex and whose holomorphic functions separate points and give local coordinates, equivalently a closed complex submanifold of some $\mathbb{C}^N$.
why: 5 catalog results name it (Andreotti–Frankel theorem, Cartan's theorems A and B); defined in nLab 'Stein manifold'. Inference: the natural domains of several complex variables (Cartan's theorems A and B).

name: Symmetric group
def: The group $S_n$ of all permutations of a set, under composition.
why: 4 catalog results name it (Abel–Ruffini theorem, Cayley's theorem); defined in Mathlib `Equiv.Perm` and nLab 'symmetric group'. Inference: the basic example of a group, appearing in combinatorics, Galois theory and physics.

name: Tensor product
def: The vector space or module $V\otimes W$ with a bilinear map $V\times W\to V\otimes W$ through which every bilinear map out of $V\times W$ factors uniquely.
why: 4 catalog results name it (Eilenberg-Watts theorem, Equational criterion for flatness); defined in Mathlib `TensorProduct` and nLab 'tensor product'. Inference: a pervasive construction of algebra, geometry and quantum physics.

name: Topological group
def: A group with a topology in which multiplication and inversion are continuous maps.
why: 1 catalog result name it (Steinhaus theorem); defined in Mathlib `IsTopologicalGroup` and nLab 'topological group'. Inference: the common setting of Lie groups, profinite groups and harmonic analysis.

name: Topological space
def: A set with a family of subsets, the open sets, that contains the empty set and the whole set and is closed under arbitrary unions and finite intersections.
why: 1 catalog result name it (metrizable space); defined in Mathlib `TopologicalSpace` and nLab 'topological space'. Inference: one of the most unifying notions of modern mathematics.

name: Tor functor
def: The left derived functors $\mathrm{Tor}_n^R(M,N)$ of the tensor product of modules, computed from a projective or flat resolution.
why: 5 catalog results name it (Künneth theorem, Serre intersection formula); no mathlib or nLab record. Inference: a basic derived functor in Künneth formulas and Serre's intersection formula.

name: Transcendental number
def: A complex number that is not a root of any nonzero polynomial with rational coefficients, such as $e$ or $\pi$.
why: 5 catalog results name it (Gelfond's theorem, Gelfond–Schneider theorem); defined in Mathlib `Transcendental` and nLab 'transcendental number'. Inference: a classical topic of number theory (Lindemann-Weierstrass, Gelfond-Schneider) with hard proofs.

name: Transversality
def: Two submanifolds, or a smooth map and a submanifold, are transverse when at each intersection point their tangent spaces together span the tangent space of the ambient manifold.
why: 5 catalog results name it (Pontryagin's theorem, Thom's theorem); no mathlib or nLab record. Inference: the genericity tool behind Thom's cobordism theory and Pontryagin's construction.

name: Unitary operator
def: A bounded linear operator $U$ on a Hilbert space with $U^*U=UU^*=I$, equivalently a surjective linear isometry.
why: 5 catalog results name it (Stone's theorem on one-parameter unitary groups, Sz.-Nagy's dilation theorem); defined in Mathlib `unitary` and nLab 'unitary operator'. Inference: the symmetries of quantum mechanics and a basic class of operators.

name: Univalent function
def: A holomorphic function that is injective on its domain, usually the unit disc.
why: 5 catalog results name it (Area theorem, Bloch's theorem); no mathlib or nLab record. Inference: the subject of geometric function theory (Bieberbach conjecture, area theorem).

name: Vector space
def: An abelian group of vectors with a multiplication by scalars from a field that is associative, unital and distributes over both additions.
why: 1 catalog result name it (basis theorem); defined in Mathlib `Module` and nLab 'vector space'. Inference: among the most unifying and applied notions of mathematics.

name: Étale cohomology
def: The sheaf cohomology of a scheme computed on its étale site, giving $\ell$-adic cohomology groups that behave like singular cohomology.
why: 5 catalog results name it (Artin–Verdier duality, Deligne's theorem); defined in nLab 'étale cohomology'. Inference: the machinery behind the Weil conjectures and arithmetic duality.

name: Abelian group
def: A group whose operation is commutative, $ab=ba$ for all elements.
why: 3 catalog results name it (Bruck-Toyoda theorem, Gabriel-Oberst duality); defined in Mathlib `CommGroup` and nLab 'abelian group'. Inference: a basic structure underlying modules, homology and number theory.

name: Adjacency matrix
def: For a graph on $n$ vertices, the $n\times n$ matrix whose $(i,j)$ entry is 1 (or the number of edges) when vertices $i$ and $j$ are adjacent and 0 otherwise.
why: 1 catalog result name it (friendship graph); defined in Mathlib `SimpleGraph.adjMatrix` and nLab 'adjacency matrix'. Inference: the bridge of spectral graph theory with wide use in network science.

name: Adjoint operator
def: For a linear operator $T$ between Hilbert spaces, the operator $T^*$ with $\langle Tx,y\rangle=\langle x,T^*y\rangle$ for all $x,y$ in the domains.
why: 1 catalog result name it (closed range theorem); defined in Mathlib `LinearPMap.adjoint` and nLab 'adjoint operator'. Inference: a basic operation of operator theory used in quantum mechanics.

name: Algebraic surface
def: An algebraic variety of dimension two.
why: 4 catalog results name it (Castelnuovo–de Franchis theorem, Hodge index theorem); defined in nLab 'algebraic surface'. Inference: the classical subject of the Enriques-Kodaira classification and the Hodge index theorem.

name: Algebraic variety
def: A space locally given as the common zero set of polynomials over an algebraically closed field, glued along Zariski-open pieces.
why: 3 catalog results name it (Chow's theorem, Riemann's existence theorem); defined in nLab 'algebraic variety'. Inference: the central object of algebraic geometry with uses in robotics, coding and statistics.

name: Automorphism group
def: The group of all isomorphisms of a mathematical object to itself, under composition.
why: 4 catalog results name it (De Franchis theorem, Frucht's theorem); no mathlib or nLab record. Inference: measures symmetry of any structure, from graphs (Frucht) to fields (Galois).

name: Banach algebra
def: An associative algebra over $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$ that is a Banach space whose norm satisfies $\|xy\|\le\|x\|\|y\|$.
why: 4 catalog results name it (Corona theorem, Gelfand's formula); defined in nLab 'Banach algebra'. Inference: the setting of Gelfand theory and spectral theory (Gelfand-Mazur, Gelfand's formula, corona theorem).

name: Bijection
def: A function that is both injective and surjective, so every element of the codomain is the image of exactly one element of the domain.
why: 3 catalog results name it (Aztec diamond, Cantor–Bernstein–Schroeder theorem); defined in Mathlib `Function.Bijective` and nLab 'bijection'. Inference: elementary and pervasive, the basis of counting and cardinality.

name: Bipartite graph
def: A graph whose vertices split into two sets so that every edge joins a vertex of one set to a vertex of the other.
why: 4 catalog results name it (Dinitz conjecture, Hall's marriage theorem); defined in nLab 'bipartite graph'. Inference: the setting of matching theory (Hall, König) with uses in scheduling and networks.

name: Borel set
def: A member of the smallest sigma-algebra on a topological space that contains all open sets.
why: 4 catalog results name it (Borel determinacy theorem, Lusin separation theorem); defined in Mathlib `borel`. Inference: the sets of measure theory and descriptive set theory (Borel determinacy, Lusin-Souslin).

name: Cardinal number
def: The size of a set, where two sets have the same cardinal exactly when there is a bijection between them.
why: 11 catalog results name it (Cantor-Schroeder-Bernstein theorem, Cantor–Bernstein–Schroeder theorem); defined in Mathlib `Cardinal` and nLab 'cardinal number'. Inference: the measure of size in set theory, eleven catalog results name it.

name: Cevian
def: A line segment joining a vertex of a triangle to a point on the line of the opposite side.
why: 4 catalog results name it (Ceva's theorem, Reuschle's theorem); no mathlib or nLab record. Inference: a narrow notion of triangle geometry (Ceva, Routh).

name: Characteristic class
def: An assignment to each vector or principal bundle over a space $X$ of a cohomology class of $X$ that is natural under pullback of bundles.
why: 3 catalog results name it (Atiyah–Singer index theorem, Riemann–Roch theorem for smooth manifolds); defined in nLab 'characteristic class'. Inference: the bridge between bundles and cohomology behind index theorems and Riemann-Roch.

name: Chern character
def: The ring homomorphism from K-theory to rational cohomology that sends a line bundle $L$ to $e^{c_1(L)}$ and is additive and multiplicative.
why: 3 catalog results name it (Grothendieck-Riemann-Roch theorem, Grothendieck–Hirzebruch–Riemann–Roch theorem); defined in nLab 'Chern character'. Inference: a specific characteristic-class construction central to Riemann-Roch-type theorems.

name: Colimit
def: For a diagram in a category, a universal cocone: an object with compatible morphisms from the diagram through which every other cocone factors uniquely.
why: 3 catalog results name it (Adámek's fixed point theorem, Eilenberg-Watts theorem); defined in Mathlib `CategoryTheory.Limits.colimit` and nLab 'colimit'. Inference: the general gluing construction of category theory, covering coproducts, pushouts and coequalizers.

name: Compact Lie group
def: A Lie group whose underlying manifold is compact, such as $U(n)$, $SO(n)$ or $SU(2)$.
why: 3 catalog results name it (Bochner linearization theorem, Weyl character formula); defined in nLab 'compact Lie group'. Inference: the groups of Weyl's character formula with uses in physics symmetry.

name: Compact space
def: A topological space in which every open cover has a finite subcover.
why: 28 catalog results name it (Alexander's subbasis theorem, Arzelà–Ascoli theorem); defined in Mathlib `CompactSpace` and nLab 'compact space'. Inference: one of the most used hypotheses in analysis and topology, 28 catalog results name it.

name: Connected space
def: A topological space that cannot be written as the union of two disjoint nonempty open sets.
why: 4 catalog results name it (First mean value theorem for set integrals (a.e. nonnegativity), Freudenthal suspension theorem); defined in Mathlib `ConnectedSpace` and nLab 'connected space'. Inference: a basic topological property used across analysis and topology.

name: Context-free language
def: A formal language generated by a context-free grammar, equivalently accepted by a nondeterministic pushdown automaton.
why: 2 catalog results name it (Chomsky–Schützenberger enumeration theorem, Chomsky–Schützenberger representation theorem); defined in Mathlib `Language.IsContextFree` and nLab 'context-free grammar'. Inference: the language class of parsing and programming-language syntax.

name: Convergence in probability
def: Random variables $X_n$ converge in probability to $X$ when $P(|X_n-X|>\varepsilon)\to0$ for every $\varepsilon>0$.
why: 1 catalog result name it (Slutsky's theorem); defined in Mathlib `MeasureTheory.TendstoInMeasure`. Inference: the mode of convergence of the weak law of large numbers and consistency in statistics.

name: de Rham cohomology
def: The cohomology of the complex of differential forms on a smooth manifold under the exterior derivative: closed forms modulo exact forms.
why: Named by Hodge theory and Lefschetz results; central bridge between analysis and topology on manifolds, with uses in gauge theory and electromagnetism (inference).

name: Diagonalizable matrix
def: A square matrix similar to a diagonal matrix, equivalently one whose eigenvectors form a basis of the underlying space.
why: Six catalog results name it (Bauer–Fike, eigendecomposition); diagonalization is used throughout numerical computing and physics.

name: Dimension of a vector space
def: The cardinality of any basis of a vector space, which is the same for all bases.
why: Used across all of linear algebra and beyond (rank–nullity, Helly); nLab's broad dimension page has many backlinks; ubiquitous in applications.

name: Diophantine equation
def: A polynomial equation with integer coefficients for which integer (or rational) solutions are sought.
why: Named by Catalan's conjecture and Pell's equation results; a defining problem class of number theory with cryptographic uses (inference).

name: Directional derivative
def: The rate of change of a function at a point along a given direction vector, the derivative of $t\mapsto f(x+tv)$ at $t=0$.
why: Mathlib defines it as lineDeriv and Danskin's theorem uses it; standard in optimization and physics.

name: Division ring
def: A ring with $1\neq 0$ in which every nonzero element has a multiplicative inverse, multiplication not necessarily commutative.
why: Named by Artin–Wedderburn and Cartan–Brauer–Hua; central in noncommutative ring theory with modest applied use (quaternions).

name: Entropy (information theory)
def: For a probability distribution $p$, the quantity $-\sum p_i\log p_i$ measuring the average information or uncertainty of a random outcome.
why: nLab entropy page with many backlinks and results such as Bregman–Minc and the H-theorem; foundational in information theory, physics, statistics and machine learning.
revised: tc-judge-revision/1: phrases narrowed after the first arXiv count showed everyday or other-field senses

name: Expected value
def: The probability-weighted average of a random variable, the integral of the variable against the probability measure.
why: Named by results across probability and applied fields; the basic quantity of probability, statistics, finance and decision theory.

name: Function of exponential type
def: An entire function $f$ with $|f(z)|\le Ae^{\tau|z|}$ for some constants $A,\tau$ and all large $|z|$.
why: Named by Carlson's and Akhiezer's theorems; organizes Paley–Wiener theory with signal-processing uses via band-limited functions (inference).

name: Exterior algebra
def: The associative algebra generated by a vector space $V$ subject to $v\wedge v=0$, whose graded pieces are the alternating powers of $V$.
why: Mathlib ExteriorAlgebra and nLab page; underlies differential forms, Koszul duality and fermionic physics.

name: Fibonacci numbers
def: The integer sequence with $F_0=0$, $F_1=1$ and $F_{n}=F_{n-1}+F_{n-2}$.
why: Named by Binet's and Cassini's identities; a classic object with uses in algorithms and modelling but narrow research role.

name: Filtration
def: An increasing family of sub-objects indexed by an ordered set; in probability, an increasing family of sigma-algebras modelling information over time.
why: Named by martingale convergence results; filtrations organize stochastic processes, spectral sequences and graded algebra (inference).

name: Flag variety
def: The projective variety parametrizing flags of subspaces of a vector space, equivalently $G/P$ for a reductive group $G$ and parabolic subgroup $P$.
why: nLab page plus Borel–Weil–Bott results; central in geometric representation theory and Schubert calculus.

name: Flat module
def: A module $M$ over a ring $R$ such that tensoring with $M$ preserves injective maps (equivalently, exact sequences).
why: nLab page and Lazard's criterion results; flatness is a cornerstone of commutative algebra and algebraic geometry.

name: Formal power series
def: An infinite formal sum $\sum a_n x^n$ with coefficients in a ring, added and multiplied like polynomials without regard to convergence.
why: Named by the Cohen structure and Artin approximation theorems; used in combinatorics, algebra and computer algebra.

name: Free module
def: A module that has a basis, so it is isomorphic to a direct sum of copies of the base ring.
why: nLab page and results such as Lazard's criterion and Leray–Hirsch; basic object of homological algebra.

name: Free product
def: The coproduct of groups: words in elements of the factors with no relations between different factors.
why: Named by the Kurosh and Grushko theorems; central in combinatorial group theory and free probability (inference).

name: Gamma function
def: The meromorphic function extending the factorial, defined by $\Gamma(s)=\int_0^\infty t^{s-1}e^{-t}\,dt$ for $\operatorname{Re}s>0$.
why: Named by Bohr–Mollerup and multiplication formula results with an nLab page; pervasive in analysis, statistics and physics.

name: Gaussian curvature
def: The product of the principal curvatures of a surface at a point, an intrinsic invariant by Gauss's Theorema Egregium.
why: Named by Hilbert's theorem and Bertrand–Diguet–Puiseux; used in differential geometry, geodesy and graphics (inference).

name: Genus of a surface
def: The number of handles of a closed orientable surface, equal to $(2-\chi)/2$ for Euler characteristic $\chi$.
why: nLab genus page and Faltings' and Harnack's theorems; the basic invariant of surfaces and curves.
revised: tc-judge-revision/1: phrases narrowed after the first arXiv count showed everyday or other-field senses

name: Grothendieck topos
def: A category equivalent to the category of sheaves of sets on a small site.
why: nLab page and Barr's and Deligne's theorems; a pillar of categorical logic and algebraic geometry with little applied use.

name: Hausdorff measure
def: For $s\ge 0$, the outer measure on a metric space obtained from covers by small sets weighted by their diameters to the power $s$.
why: Mathlib hausdorffMeasure and the analyst's traveling salesman theorem; core of geometric measure theory and fractal geometry.

name: Homeomorphism
def: A continuous bijection between topological spaces whose inverse is also continuous.
why: nLab page and results such as Alexander's trick and Hartman–Grobman; the notion of sameness throughout topology.

name: Homotopy
def: A continuous deformation between two maps $f,g:X\to Y$, given by a map $H:X\times[0,1]\to Y$ with $H_0=f$ and $H_1=g$.
why: nLab page and the monodromy theorem; the foundational relation of algebraic topology.

name: Homotopy colimit
def: A colimit construction that is invariant under weak equivalences, the derived version of the colimit of a diagram.
why: Named by the Bousfield–Kan formula and higher van Kampen results; key tool in modern homotopy theory.

name: Integer
def: A whole number: an element of $\mathbb Z=\{\dots,-2,-1,0,1,2,\dots\}$.
why: nLab page and number theory results (Bézout, four squares); the integers underlie all of mathematics and computing.

name: Integrable function
def: A measurable function whose absolute value has finite Lebesgue integral.
why: Named by Fubini's theorem and Fourier series results; integrability hypotheses run through analysis and probability.

name: Jacobian matrix
def: The matrix of first-order partial derivatives of a differentiable map between Euclidean spaces.
why: Eight catalog results name it (constant rank theorem, stability results); central to optimization, robotics and numerical methods.

name: Jacobian variety
def: The abelian variety parametrizing degree-zero divisor classes on a smooth projective curve.
why: nLab page and results such as Abel–Jacobi and Manin–Drinfeld; key object in arithmetic geometry with cryptographic uses (inference).

name: Jordan algebra
def: A commutative, generally nonassociative algebra satisfying the Jordan identity $(xy)(xx)=x(y(xx))$.
why: nLab page and operator-algebra results (Alfsen–Shultz); a specialized structure with links to quantum mechanics.

name: Kernel of a homomorphism
def: The set of elements a homomorphism sends to the identity (zero) element.
why: nLab kernel page and the isomorphism theorems; used across algebra and in linear-algebra applications.

name: L-function
def: A meromorphic function given by a Dirichlet series with an Euler product, attached to arithmetic or automorphic data.
why: nLab page and Chebotarev and Dirichlet results; L-functions drive the Langlands program but have little applied use.

name: Loop space
def: The space of based loops in a pointed topological space, with the compact-open topology.
why: nLab page and the James construction and May recognition theorem; central in homotopy theory and string topology.

name: Lorentz group
def: The group $O(1,3)$ of linear maps of Minkowski space preserving the quadratic form $t^2-x^2-y^2-z^2$.
why: nLab page and the PCT theorem; fundamental in special relativity and particle physics.

name: Markov chain
def: A stochastic process whose next state depends only on the current state, given by transition probabilities.
why: nLab page and the Chapman–Kolmogorov equation and Foster's theorem; heavily used in statistics, physics, finance and computing.

name: Matrix
def: A rectangular array of entries from a ring, representing a linear map in chosen bases.
why: nLab page and Cayley–Hamilton and Gaussian elimination; the basic tool of applied mathematics, science and engineering.

name: Model category
def: A category with three classes of maps (weak equivalences, fibrations, cofibrations) satisfying lifting, factorization and limit axioms.
why: nLab page and Bousfield–Friedlander and Strøm theorems; the standard framework of abstract homotopy theory.

name: Modular representation
def: A linear representation of a finite group over a field whose characteristic divides the group order.
why: Named by Brauer's main theorems and Brauer–Nesbitt; a core area of finite group representation theory.

name: Morava K-theory
def: A family of complex-oriented cohomology theories $K(n)$, at a prime $p$, whose coefficient ring is $\mathbb F_p[v_n^{\pm1}]$.
why: nLab page and the nilpotence and chromatic convergence theorems; central to chromatic homotopy theory only.

name: Noetherian module
def: A module in which every ascending chain of submodules stabilizes, equivalently every submodule is finitely generated.
why: Mathlib IsNoetherian and nLab page with Orzech's theorem; a standard finiteness condition in commutative algebra.

name: NP (complexity class)
def: The class of decision problems whose yes-instances have certificates verifiable by a deterministic Turing machine in polynomial time.
why: nLab page and Cook–Levin and Karp–Lipton theorems; NP-hardness classifies problems across computing and operations research.

name: Order of an element
def: The least positive integer $n$ with $g^n=e$ for a group element $g$, or infinity if none exists.
why: Mathlib orderOf and Cauchy's group theorem; basic in group theory and cryptography.

name: Order topology
def: The topology on a totally ordered set generated by the open rays $\{x<a\}$ and $\{x>a\}$.
why: Mathlib OrderTopology and nLab page, with a result on monotone functions; a narrow construction in general topology.

name: Ordinal
def: The order type of a well-ordered set; ordinals extend the natural numbers into the transfinite.
why: Mathlib Ordinal and the Burali-Forti paradox; ordinals underlie set theory, proof theory and transfinite induction.

name: Orthogonal projection
def: The linear map sending each vector of an inner product space to its nearest point in a closed subspace.
why: Mathlib orthogonalProjection and the mean ergodic theorem; used in least squares, signal processing and quantum mechanics.

name: Orthonormal basis
def: A set of mutually orthogonal unit vectors whose span is dense in an inner product space.
why: Named by Parseval's identity and Karhunen–Loève; ubiquitous in signal processing, quantum physics and numerics.

name: Paracompact space
def: A Hausdorff topological space in which every open cover has a locally finite open refinement.
why: Named by Michael's selection theorems; a key hypothesis for partitions of unity in topology and geometry.

name: Perverse sheaf
def: An object of the derived category of constructible sheaves satisfying support and cosupport conditions, the heart of the perverse t-structure.
why: nLab page and the BBDG decomposition and Riemann–Hilbert results; central in geometric representation theory, no applied use.

name: Prime spectrum
def: The set of prime ideals of a commutative ring, with the Zariski topology.
why: Mathlib PrimeSpectrum, nLab page and Chevalley's theorem; the foundation of scheme theory.

name: Principal ideal domain
def: An integral domain in which every ideal is generated by a single element.
why: nLab page and the structure theorem for modules over a PID; a standard class in algebra and number theory.

name: Probability density function
def: A nonnegative function whose integral over a set gives the probability that a random variable lies in that set.
why: Mathlib HasPDF and the law of the unconscious statistician; densities are basic in statistics, physics and engineering.

name: Product topology
def: The coarsest topology on a Cartesian product of spaces making every coordinate projection continuous.
why: Named by Tychonoff's theorem and pointwise convergence; a standard construction in general topology.

name: Projective space
def: The space of lines through the origin in a vector space, $\mathbb P(V)=(V\setminus 0)/\text{scalars}$.
why: nLab page and results such as the subspace theorem and Wigner's theorem; used in geometry, physics and computer vision.

name: Proper map
def: A continuous map under which preimages of compact sets are compact (in algebraic geometry, separated, finite type and universally closed).
why: Seven catalog results name it (BBDG, Ehresmann) and nLab defines it; a key hypothesis in topology and algebraic geometry.

name: Pullback (category theory)
def: The limit of a diagram $X\to Z\leftarrow Y$: a universal object with maps to $X$ and $Y$ agreeing in $Z$.
why: nLab page and Schanuel's lemma; pullbacks are pervasive in category theory and geometry and appear in type theory and databases (inference).

name: Quadrilateral
def: A polygon with four sides and four vertices.
why: Named by Euler's and Anne's quadrilateral theorems; an elementary figure with mesh-generation uses but narrow research role.

name: Quantum group
def: A Hopf algebra deforming the universal enveloping algebra of a Lie algebra or the function algebra of a group.
why: nLab page and Drinfeld–Kohno and Kazhdan–Lusztig results; central in quantum algebra with uses in integrable systems.

name: Quaternion
def: An element $a+bi+cj+dk$ of the four-dimensional real division algebra with $i^2=j^2=k^2=ijk=-1$.
why: nLab page and the Cayley–Dickson construction; used heavily for 3D rotations in graphics, robotics and aerospace.

name: Rational number
def: A number expressible as a quotient $p/q$ of integers with $q\neq0$.
why: nLab page and irrationality results; the rationals are basic throughout mathematics and computation.

name: Regular space
def: A topological space in which any point and closed set not containing it have disjoint open neighbourhoods.
why: Named by the Bing and Nagata–Smirnov metrization theorems; a separation axiom of general topology.

name: Ricci curvature
def: The trace of the Riemann curvature tensor, a symmetric 2-tensor measuring volume distortion along geodesics.
