why: nLab page and comparison theorems (Cheeger–Gromoll, Cheng); central in geometric analysis and general relativity.

name: Boolean satisfiability problem
def: The decision problem of whether a given propositional formula has an assignment of truth values making it true.
why: The packet's mathlib match is first-order satisfiability, not SAT; from knowledge, SAT is the first NP-complete problem and SAT solvers are used across verification and planning.

name: Schwartz space
def: The space of smooth functions on $\mathbb R^n$ all of whose derivatives decay faster than any polynomial.
why: Mathlib SchwartzMap, nLab page and the Fourier inversion theorem; the standard domain for Fourier analysis and distributions.

name: Sheaf
def: A presheaf on a space or site whose sections agree locally can be uniquely glued into global sections.
why: nLab page and Giraud's theorem; sheaves organize algebraic geometry, topology and logic, with emerging data-science uses.

name: Simplicial set
def: A functor from the opposite of the simplex category to sets, a combinatorial model of spaces.
why: nLab page and Eilenberg–Zilber and Sullivan results; the combinatorial basis of homotopy theory and higher categories.

name: Square (geometry)
def: A quadrilateral with four equal sides and four right angles.
why: Named by Finsler–Hadwiger and Thébault theorems; elementary and ubiquitous but a narrow research object.
revised: tc-judge-revision/1: phrases narrowed after the first arXiv count showed everyday or other-field senses

name: Substructure
def: A subset of a structure closed under its operations and containing its constants, with the induced relations.
why: Mathlib FirstOrder.Language.Substructure and the Tarski–Vaught test; a basic notion of model theory.

name: Sufficient statistic
def: A statistic such that the conditional distribution of the data given it does not depend on the unknown parameter.
why: Named by Basu's and Lehmann–Scheffé theorems; a core notion of mathematical statistics.

name: Surface (topology)
def: A two-dimensional topological manifold.
why: nLab page and Gauss–Bonnet and Dehn–Nielsen–Baer; surfaces appear across geometry, topology and graphics.
revised: tc-judge-revision/1: phrases narrowed after the first arXiv count showed everyday or other-field senses

name: Suspension (topology)
def: The space $SX$ obtained from $X\times[0,1]$ by collapsing each end to a point.
why: nLab page and the Freudenthal suspension theorem; a basic construction of homotopy theory.

name: Ultrafilter
def: A maximal proper filter on a set or lattice: for every subset, either it or its complement belongs to the filter.
why: nLab page and Stone's representation theorem; used in topology, model theory and Ramsey theory.

name: Weak factorization system
def: A pair of classes of morphisms such that every map factors as one followed by the other and each class is the lifting complement of the other.
why: nLab page and the small object and retract arguments; a technical backbone of model categories.

name: Čech cohomology
def: Cohomology computed from cochains on the nerves of open covers, passing to the limit over refinements.
why: nLab page and Leray's theorem and Alexander–Čech duality; a standard computational cohomology in topology and geometry.

name: Algebraic theory (universal algebra)
def: A signature of operations with equational axioms, whose models are algebras such as groups or rings.
why: nLab page and Lawvere reconstruction results; organizes universal algebra with uses in computer science semantics.

name: Analytic continuation
def: The extension of a holomorphic function beyond its original domain to a larger domain, unique where it exists.
why: nLab page and monodromy and gap theorems; crucial for zeta functions and physics amplitudes.

name: Antichain
def: A subset of a partially ordered set in which no two distinct elements are comparable.
why: nLab page and Dilworth and LYM results; a basic object of extremal combinatorics.

name: Automorphic form
def: A function on a Lie group invariant under a discrete subgroup, satisfying growth and differential conditions; generalizes modular forms.
why: nLab page and the Arthur–Selberg trace formula and Lafforgue's theorem; heart of the Langlands program.

name: Bernoulli number
def: The rational numbers $B_n$ defined by the generating function $t/(e^t-1)=\sum B_n t^n/n!$.
why: Mathlib bernoulli, nLab page and Euler–Maclaurin and Herbrand–Ribet; important in number theory and summation.

name: Bicategory
def: A weak 2-category: objects, morphisms and 2-morphisms with composition associative and unital only up to coherent isomorphism.
why: nLab page and strictification results; a basic tool of higher category theory.

name: Bousfield localization
def: A localization of a homotopy theory or model category that inverts a chosen class of maps, such as the equivalences of a homology theory.
why: nLab page and Bousfield–Friedlander and chromatic convergence; a research-level tool of homotopy theory.

name: Chromatic number
def: The least number of colours needed to colour the vertices of a graph so that adjacent vertices differ.
why: Named by Brooks' and Erdős–Stone theorems; a central graph invariant with scheduling and register-allocation uses.

name: Ideal class group
def: The group of fractional ideals of a Dedekind domain modulo principal ones; its order is the class number.
why: Seven catalog results (class number formula, Ankeny–Artin–Chowla) and an nLab page; measures failure of unique factorization.

name: Clique (graph theory)
def: A set of vertices of a graph that are pairwise adjacent.
why: nLab page and Turán's theorem; cliques matter in extremal combinatorics, complexity and network analysis.

name: Commutant
def: The set of operators commuting with every element of a given set of operators.
why: nLab page and the bicommutant and Fuglede theorems; central to von Neumann algebra theory.

name: Compact convex set
def: A convex subset of a topological vector space that is also compact.
why: Named by Ryll-Nardzewski and Sion's minimax theorems; used in optimization and game theory.

name: Compact metric space
def: A metric space in which every sequence has a convergent subsequence.
why: Named by the Lebesgue number lemma and Hausdorff–Alexandroff; a standard setting across analysis and dynamics.

name: Complex cobordism
def: The generalized cohomology theory $MU$ built from cobordism classes of stably complex manifolds.
why: Named by Landweber exact functor and Landweber–Novikov theorems; the foundation of chromatic homotopy theory.

name: Contraction mapping
def: A map of a metric space with $d(f(x),f(y))\le k\,d(x,y)$ for some constant $k<1$.
why: nLab page and the Banach fixed-point theorem; used in numerical analysis, ODE theory and dynamic programming.

name: Coprime integers
def: Integers whose greatest common divisor is 1.
why: nLab page and McNugget and Pythagorean triple results; elementary number theory with cryptographic uses.

name: Dedekind zeta function
def: The zeta function of a number field, $\zeta_K(s)=\sum_{\mathfrak a}N(\mathfrak a)^{-s}$ over nonzero ideals of its ring of integers.
why: nLab page and the class number formula and Landau prime ideal theorem; central in algebraic number theory.

name: Digamma function
def: The logarithmic derivative of the gamma function, $\psi(x)=\Gamma'(x)/\Gamma(x)$.
why: Named by reflection and duplication formula results; a special function with uses in statistics but narrow reach.

name: Direct product
def: The set of tuples drawn from a family of algebraic structures, with the operations applied componentwise.
why: Named by structure results such as Goursat's lemma and the finite abelian group theorem; nLab defines it with 25 backlinks. Breadth across algebra is inferred.

name: Distribution function
def: For a real random variable $X$, the function $F(x)=P(X\le x)$, which is non-decreasing, right-continuous and determines the law of $X$.
why: Underlies Helly-Bray and extreme value results; ubiquitous in statistics (inference).

name: Divisor function
def: The arithmetic function $\sigma_k(n)=\sum_{d\mid n} d^k$, summing the $k$-th powers of the positive divisors of $n$.
why: Named by the Euclid-Euler and perfect number results; a classical arithmetic function of number theory.

name: E-infinity ring
def: A spectrum with a multiplication that is associative and commutative up to coherent higher homotopies, governed by an $E_\infty$ operad.
why: Named by Goerss-Hopkins-Miller and red-shift results; central to modern stable homotopy theory (inference), no applied use.

name: Eisenstein series
def: A modular form of weight $k$ obtained by summing $(c\tau+d)^{-k}$ over coprime integer pairs $(c,d)$.
why: Named by Ramanujan's formulas for E2, E4, E6; nLab page exists; basic building block of modular forms.

name: Elliptic operator
def: A linear differential operator whose principal symbol is invertible at every nonzero cotangent vector.
why: Named by the Atiyah-Singer index theorem and Hodge theorem; elliptic PDE also model physical equilibria (inference).

name: Exact functor
def: A functor between abelian (or triangulated) categories that sends exact sequences to exact sequences.
why: Named by the Freyd-Mitchell embedding theorem; nLab page with 101 backlinks; core notion of homological algebra.

name: Factorial
def: For a natural number $n$, the product $n!=1\cdot2\cdots n$ (with $0!=1$), which counts the orderings of $n$ objects.
why: Named by Stirling, Wilson and Legendre results; used throughout combinatorics, probability and computing.

name: Fibration
def: A map with the homotopy lifting property (Hurewicz or Serre), or more generally a member of the fibration class of a model category.
why: nLab page with 127 backlinks; organizes long exact sequences of homotopy groups; the word also names algebraic-geometric fibrations (packet example).

name: Fibre bundle
def: A continuous surjection $E\to B$ that over small open sets of $B$ looks like the projection $U\times F\to U$.
why: Named by Ehresmann and Leray-Hirsch theorems; gauge theory in physics is built on bundles.

name: Finite measure
def: A measure that gives the whole space finite total mass.
why: Hypothesis of Egorov, bounded convergence and Poincaré recurrence; probability measures are the normalized case.

name: Finite-dimensional vector space
def: A vector space that has a finite basis, equivalently is spanned by finitely many vectors.
why: Setting of eigenvalue existence and orthonormal bases results; the arena of all applied linear algebra.

name: Floor function
def: The function sending a real number $x$ to the greatest integer $\lfloor x\rfloor$ that is at most $x$.
why: Named by Beatty sequence, Hermite and Legendre results; ubiquitous in computing.

name: Galois cohomology
def: The cohomology of a profinite Galois group acting continuously on a discrete module.
why: Named by Hilbert 90 and the norm residue isomorphism theorem; nLab page; central in arithmetic geometry.

name: Galois extension
def: An algebraic field extension that is normal and separable, so the field fixed by its automorphism group is exactly the base field.
why: Named by the Galois correspondence and Chebotarev density; mathlib and nLab define it; coding theory uses finite Galois extensions.

name: Geometric morphism
def: A pair of adjoint functors between toposes whose left adjoint, the inverse image, preserves finite limits.
why: Named by Barr and Diaconescu theorems; nLab page with 165 backlinks; the morphisms of topos theory.

name: Golden ratio
def: The number $\varphi=(1+\sqrt5)/2$, the positive root of $x^2=x+1$.
why: Named by Binet's formula and pentagon identities; mostly a recreational and geometric constant.

name: Graph minor
def: A graph obtained from another graph by deleting vertices or edges and contracting edges.
why: Named by Robertson-Seymour and Wagner theorems; the graph minor theory drives parameterized algorithms.

name: Hamiltonian cycle
def: A cycle in a graph that passes through every vertex exactly once.
why: Named by Ore and Grinberg theorems; NP-complete decision problem linked to routing (TSP).

name: Highest weight
def: For a representation of a semisimple Lie algebra, a weight whose weight vector is killed by all positive root vectors; it classifies the irreducible finite-dimensional representations.
why: Named by Borel-Weil-Bott and the Weyl character formula; also organizes particle multiplets in physics (inference).

name: Holomorphic vector bundle
def: A complex vector bundle over a complex manifold whose transition functions are holomorphic.
why: Named by Birkhoff-Grothendieck and the Oka principle; nLab page; central in complex geometry.

name: Hyperbolic 3-manifold
def: A 3-manifold carrying a complete Riemannian metric of constant sectional curvature $-1$.
why: Named by the tameness and virtual fibering theorems; geometrization made them central to 3-manifold topology.

name: Hyperplane section
def: The intersection of a projective variety with a hyperplane of its ambient projective space.
why: Named by the Lefschetz hyperplane theorem and Bertini; a standard tool of projective geometry.

name: Immersion
def: A smooth map between manifolds whose differential is injective at every point.
why: Named by Whitney immersion theorem and regular homotopy; nLab page; the word also has non-mathematical senses.

name: Integer partition
def: A way of writing a positive integer as an unordered sum of positive integers.
why: Named by the pentagonal number theorem and Glaisher; indexes representations of symmetric groups (inference).

name: Integral extension
def: A ring extension $A\subseteq B$ in which every element of $B$ is a root of a monic polynomial with coefficients in $A$.
why: Named by going-up/going-down and Noether normalization; foundation of algebraic number theory.

name: Intersecting family
def: A family of sets in which every two members share at least one element.
why: Named by Erdős-Ko-Rado and Kleitman theorems; a core object of extremal set theory.

name: Intersection multiplicity
def: A positive integer measuring how many times two subvarieties meet at a common point, e.g. the length of a local quotient ring.
why: Named by Bézout's theorem and Serre's intersection formula; a standard invariant of intersection theory.

name: Interval (real line)
def: A subset of the real line that contains every number lying between two of its members.
why: Named by the intermediate value theorem; nLab page with 120 backlinks; used everywhere.

name: Intuitionistic logic
def: A logic without the law of excluded middle, in which proving a statement means constructing evidence for it.
why: Named by the double-negation translation; nLab page; underlies type theory and proof assistants.

name: Involution
def: A map that is its own inverse, so applying it twice gives the identity.
why: Named by the Z* theorem and Pappus involution; nLab page with 108 backlinks.

name: Jet bundle
def: The bundle whose fibres record the Taylor expansions up to a given order of local sections of a fibre bundle.
why: Named by Thom transversality and the h-principle; nLab page; used in the geometry of PDE and field theory.

name: Laurent series
def: A series $\sum_{n\in\mathbb Z} a_n (z-c)^n$ that may include negative powers, used to expand a function around an isolated singularity.
why: Named by the residue theorem and Casorati-Weierstrass; nLab page.

name: Least upper bound (supremum)
def: The smallest element that is greater than or equal to every element of a given subset of an ordered set.
why: Named by the Archimedean property and nested intervals results; completeness of the reals rests on it.

name: Legendre symbol
def: For an odd prime $p$, the symbol $(a/p)$ equal to $1$, $-1$ or $0$ as $a$ is a nonzero square, a non-square or zero modulo $p$.
why: Named by quadratic reciprocity and Gauss's and Eisenstein's lemmas; used in primality tests and cryptography.

name: Loop group
def: The group of smooth maps from the circle into a Lie group under pointwise multiplication.
why: Named by Birkhoff decomposition and the Kac character formula; nLab page; used in conformal field theory.

name: Lower semicontinuous function
def: A function $f$ with $\liminf_{y\to x} f(y)\ge f(x)$ at every point, equivalently with every set $\{f>t\}$ open.
why: Named by Caristi and Fenchel-Moreau theorems; a standard hypothesis in optimization.

name: Mahler measure
def: For a polynomial, the absolute value of its leading coefficient times the product of the absolute values of its roots lying outside the unit circle.
why: Named by Landau, Mignotte and Northcott results; a height function of Diophantine geometry.

name: Markov kernel
def: A measurable family $\kappa(x,\cdot)$ of probability measures on one space indexed by the points of another.
why: Named by Chapman-Kolmogorov, Ionescu-Tulcea and data processing results; nLab page; the transition law of Markov models.

name: Measure-preserving map
def: A measurable map $T$ between measure spaces such that the preimage of every measurable set has the same measure as the set.
why: Named by Poincaré recurrence and the maximal ergodic theorem; the basic object of ergodic theory.

name: Modal logic
def: A logic that extends propositional logic with operators $\Box$ and $\Diamond$ for necessity and possibility, interpreted in relational (Kripke) frames.
why: Named by Goldblatt-Thomason and Sahlqvist results; nLab page; used in verification and AI.

name: Moment generating function
def: For a random variable $X$, the function $t\mapsto E[e^{tX}]$, whose derivatives at $0$ are the moments of $X$.
why: Named by Chernoff, Hoeffding and Cramér results; standard tool in statistics.

name: Normal space
def: A topological space in which any two disjoint closed sets have disjoint open neighbourhoods.
why: Named by Urysohn's lemma and Tietze extension; a separation axiom of general topology.

name: Open set
def: A member of the chosen family of sets of a topology; in a metric space, a set that contains a ball around each of its points.
why: Named by Baire category and maximum modulus results; the basic notion of topology.

name: p-adic number
def: An element of $\mathbb Q_p$, the completion of the rationals for the absolute value $|x|_p=p^{-v_p(x)}$.
why: Named by Hasse-Minkowski, Ostrowski and Ax-Kochen; mathlib and nLab define it; pervasive in number theory.

name: Parallelogram
def: A quadrilateral whose two pairs of opposite sides are parallel.
why: Named by Pappus area and Euler quadrilateral theorems; elementary geometry with uses in vector addition.

name: Partial derivative
def: The derivative of a function of several variables with respect to one variable, the others held fixed.
why: Named by Green's theorem, Cauchy-Riemann and implicit function results; used in all of science and engineering.

name: Polish space
def: A separable topological space whose topology comes from some complete metric.
why: Named by Lusin-Souslin and the disintegration theorem; nLab page; the setting of descriptive set theory and probability.

name: Polynomial hierarchy
def: The hierarchy of complexity classes $\Sigma_k^P$ and $\Pi_k^P$ defined by polynomial-time computation with $k$ alternating quantifiers or nested NP oracles.
why: Named by Toda, Karp-Lipton and Sipser-Lautemann theorems; a central structure of complexity theory.

name: Pontryagin dual
def: The group of continuous homomorphisms from a locally compact abelian group to the circle group, with the compact-open topology.
why: Named by Cartier and Brown-Comenetz dualities; abstract harmonic analysis rests on it.

name: Positive linear functional
def: A linear functional on an ordered vector space or $*$-algebra that is non-negative on positive elements.
why: Named by GNS, Riesz-Markov-Kakutani and M. Riesz extension; states in quantum mechanics are positive functionals (inference).

name: Projective variety
def: A closed subvariety of projective space defined by homogeneous polynomial equations.
why: Named by Bertini, Borel fixed point and Fulton-Hansen theorems; nLab page; the main objects of classical algebraic geometry.

name: Pseudoholomorphic curve
def: A smooth map from a Riemann surface into an almost complex manifold whose differential is complex linear.
why: Named by Gromov compactness and non-squeezing; nLab page; foundation of Floer theory and Gromov-Witten invariants.

name: q-expansion
def: The Fourier expansion $\sum a_n q^n$ with $q=e^{2\pi i\tau}$ of a modular form at a cusp.
al: Fourier expansion of a modular form
why: Named by Sturm and Hecke bounds; the standard way to compute with modular forms.

name: Quadratic residue
def: An integer that is congruent to a perfect square modulo a given modulus.
why: Named by Gauss's lemma, Proth's theorem and the Paley construction; used in cryptography and design theory.

name: Random variable
def: A measurable function from a probability space to a measurable space, usually the real numbers.
why: Named by the laws of large numbers and the central limit theorem; nLab page; the basic object of probability and statistics.

name: Rational function
def: A quotient $p/q$ of two polynomials, with $q$ not the zero polynomial.
why: Named by Runge, Weil reciprocity and partial fractions; nLab page; used in control and signal processing.

name: Reflective subcategory
def: A full subcategory whose inclusion functor has a left adjoint.
why: Named by Day's reflection theorem and Gabriel-Popescu; nLab page with 202 backlinks.

name: Regular polygon
def: A polygon whose sides are all equal and whose angles are all equal.
why: Named by Platonic solid results; nLab page; elementary geometry.

name: Regulator (number theory)
def: For a number field, the covolume of its unit group modulo torsion under the logarithmic embedding, computed as a determinant of logarithms of fundamental units.
why: Named by the class number formula and Brauer-Siegel; a standard invariant of algebraic number theory.

name: Relation
def: A subset of a Cartesian product $A\times B$, recording which pairs of elements are related.
why: Named by Dowker duality; nLab page with 188 backlinks; foundational, used in databases (relational model).

name: Representable functor
def: A set-valued functor naturally isomorphic to a hom-functor $\mathrm{Hom}(X,-)$ or $\mathrm{Hom}(-,X)$.
why: Named by Brown representability; nLab page with 274 backlinks; central via the Yoneda lemma and moduli problems.

name: Ricci flow
def: The evolution equation $\partial_t g=-2\,\mathrm{Ric}(g)$ that deforms a Riemannian metric by its Ricci curvature.
why: Named by the Poincaré and geometrization conjectures; nLab page; a major research direction in geometric analysis.

name: Riemann zeta function
def: The function $\zeta(s)=\sum_{n\ge1} n^{-s}$ for $\mathrm{Re}\,s>1$, continued meromorphically to the complex plane with a single pole at $s=1$.
why: Named by the prime number theorem and Apéry's theorem; mathlib and nLab define it; also appears in physics (inference).

name: Sequence
def: A function from the natural numbers (or an initial segment of them) to a set, listing terms $a_0,a_1,a_2,\dots$.
why: Named by Bolzano-Weierstrass and Erdős-Szekeres; nLab page with 135 backlinks; basic everywhere.

name: Serre derivative
def: The operator $\vartheta_k f=f'-\tfrac{k}{12}E_2 f$ that sends modular forms of weight $k$ to modular forms of weight $k+2$.
why: Named only by Ramanujan's formulas for E2, E4, E6; a narrow tool of modular form theory.

name: Signed measure
def: A countably additive real-valued set function on a sigma-algebra, allowed to take negative values.
why: Named by the Hahn, Jordan and Lebesgue decomposition theorems; dual of continuous functions (inference).

name: Simply connected space
def: A path-connected space in which every loop can be continuously shrunk to a point, i.e. whose fundamental group is trivial.
why: Named by six results incl. Cauchy's integral theorem and Lie's third theorem; nLab page.

name: Grothendieck site
def: A category equipped with a Grothendieck topology, which declares certain families of morphisms into each object to be covers.
why: Named by Giraud's theorem and the comparison lemma; nLab page with 420 backlinks; basis of étale cohomology.

name: Spin manifold
def: An oriented Riemannian manifold with a spin structure, a lift of its frame bundle to the spin group; one exists iff the second Stiefel-Whitney class vanishes.
why: Named by Rokhlin, Lichnerowicz and Furuta theorems; needed to define fermions in physics (inference).

name: Stabilizer (group action)
def: For a group acting on a set, the subgroup of group elements that fix a given point.
why: Named by the class formula and Kneser's theorem; with orbits it organizes all group actions.

name: Subalgebra
def: A subset of an algebra that contains the unit and is closed under addition, multiplication and scalar multiplication, hence an algebra itself.
why: Named by Stone-Weierstrass and Birkhoff's HSP theorem; nLab page.

name: Subsequence
def: A sequence $(a_{n_k})$ obtained from $(a_n)$ by keeping infinitely many terms in order, with $n_1<n_2<\cdots$.
why: Named by Bolzano-Weierstrass and sequential compactness; finite subsequences also appear in string algorithms.

name: Sylow subgroup
def: For a prime $p$, a subgroup of a finite group whose order is the largest power of $p$ dividing the group's order.
why: Named by Burnside's normal p-complement and focal subgroup theorems; core of finite group theory.

name: Taylor series
def: The power series $\sum_n f^{(n)}(a)(x-a)^n/n!$ formed from the derivatives of a smooth function at a point.
why: Named by Euler-Maclaurin and quasi-analytic results; nLab page; approximation everywhere in science.

name: Thom spectrum
def: The spectrum built from the Thom spaces of a compatible family of vector bundles, such as $MO$ or $MU$, whose homotopy groups compute cobordism.
why: Named by Thom's theorem and the Mumford conjecture; nLab page with 108 backlinks.

name: Todd class
def: The characteristic class of a complex vector bundle given multiplicatively by $x/(1-e^{-x})$ in its Chern roots.
why: Named by Hirzebruch-Riemann-Roch and Grothendieck-Riemann-Roch; nLab page.

name: Tree (graph theory)
def: A connected graph that contains no cycles.
why: Named by Kruskal's tree theorem and Kőnig's lemma; nLab page; ubiquitous in computer science.

name: Ultraproduct
def: The quotient of a product of structures that identifies two tuples when they agree on a set belonging to a fixed ultrafilter.
why: Named by Łoś's theorem and Ax-Kochen; nLab page.

name: Universal enveloping algebra
def: The associative unital algebra $U(\mathfrak g)$ universally generated by a Lie algebra $\mathfrak g$ so that commutators realize its bracket.
why: Named by Poincaré-Birkhoff-Witt and Milnor-Moore; mathlib and nLab define it; used in quantum physics (inference).

name: Weak convergence
def: Convergence $x_n\to x$ tested against continuous linear functionals, or for measures against integrals of bounded continuous functions.
why: Named by Donsker, Helly-Bray and Skorokhod theorems; basic in statistics asymptotics and PDE.

name: Weak topology
def: The coarsest topology on a topological vector space that makes every continuous linear functional continuous.
why: Named by Eberlein-Šmulian and Orlicz-Pettis; nLab page.

name: Weak-star topology
def: The coarsest topology on a dual space that makes evaluation at each vector continuous.
why: Named by Banach-Alaoglu-type results such as Goldstine and Krein-Šmulian.

name: Weyl group
def: The finite group generated by the reflections in the roots of a root system, equivalently $N(T)/T$ for a maximal torus $T$ of a compact Lie group.
why: Named by Bruhat decomposition, Springer correspondence and the Weyl character formula; nLab page.

name: 2-category
def: A category enriched in categories: objects, morphisms, and 2-morphisms between morphisms, with strictly associative compositions.
why: nLab page with 442 backlinks but only one catalog result; a basic notion of higher category theory.

name: Absolute value
def: A multiplicative, subadditive map from a field to the non-negative reals that vanishes only at zero; the basic case is $|x|$ on the real numbers.
why: Named by Ostrowski's theorem; mathlib and nLab define it; used everywhere.

name: Automorphism
def: An isomorphism from a mathematical object to itself.
why: One catalog result but nLab page with 120 backlinks; symmetry is a unifying idea across mathematics.

name: Bimodule
def: An abelian group that is a left module over one ring and a right module over another, with the two actions commuting.
why: Named by Eilenberg-Watts; nLab page with 104 backlinks; Morita theory and subfactors use it.

name: Braided monoidal category
def: A monoidal category with natural isomorphisms $X\otimes Y\cong Y\otimes X$ satisfying the hexagon identities.
why: Named by the Kazhdan-Lusztig correspondence; nLab page; used for anyons and topological quantum computing.

name: Cartesian closed category
def: A category with finite products in which each functor $-\times X$ has a right adjoint, the exponential $(-)^X$.
why: Named by Lawvere's fixed point theorem; nLab page with 215 backlinks; semantics of typed lambda calculus.

name: Cartesian monoidal category
def: A monoidal category whose tensor product is the categorical product and whose unit is a terminal object.
why: Named by Fox's theorem; nLab page with 203 backlinks.

name: Classifying topos
def: A topos $S[T]$ such that geometric morphisms from any topos $E$ into it correspond naturally to models of a geometric theory $T$ in $E$.
al: classifying space of a geometric theory
why: Central in topos-theoretic model theory (Caramello's bridges); one catalog result (Diaconescu) and an nLab page with 105 backlinks; no applied use.

name: Closed monoidal category
def: A monoidal category in which tensoring with each object has a right adjoint, the internal hom.
why: Organizes internal homs across algebra, logic and semantics of programming (inference); one catalog result and a well-linked nLab page (229 backlinks).

name: Cocycle
def: An element of a cochain group whose coboundary vanishes; more broadly, a map satisfying a compatibility identity such as $c(gh)=c(g)+g\cdot c(h)$ for a group action.
why: Used across cohomology, ergodic theory (Oseledets) and gauge theory; nLab page with 208 backlinks; one catalog result.

name: Cohomotopy
def: The contravariant functor sending a space $X$ to the set of homotopy classes of maps from $X$ to a sphere $S^n$.
why: A classical but specialized invariant (Pontryagin's theorem, Bauer-Furuta invariants); one catalog result and nLab page; some speculative use in M-theory.

name: Complex manifold
def: A manifold covered by charts to open sets of $\mathbb{C}^n$ whose transition maps are holomorphic.
why: Basic object of complex geometry, used in algebraic geometry and string theory; nLab page and one catalog result.

name: Discrete group
def: A topological group carrying the discrete topology, or a subgroup of a Lie group whose induced topology is discrete.
why: Discrete subgroups of Lie groups (lattices, Kleinian groups) organize geometric group theory; nLab page with 168 backlinks and one result (Kan-Thurston).

name: Endofunctor
def: A functor from a category to itself.
why: Underlies monads, initial algebras and coalgebras used in programming semantics; nLab page and one result (Adamek's fixed point theorem).

name: Enriched category
def: A category whose hom-objects lie in a monoidal category $V$, with composition and identities given by morphisms of $V$.
why: Frames additive, simplicial, metric and higher categories alike; nLab page with 410 backlinks and the enriched Yoneda lemma in the catalog.

name: Equivalence class
def: The set of all elements related to a given element by an equivalence relation.
why: A basic construction used for every quotient object across mathematics and computing; nLab page and one result (Scott's trick).

name: Equivalence relation
def: A binary relation that is reflexive, symmetric and transitive.
why: Fundamental for quotients everywhere, from modular arithmetic to automata (Myhill-Nerode); nLab page with 273 backlinks.

name: Equivariant cohomology
def: The cohomology of the homotopy quotient $EG\times_G X$ of a $G$-space $X$, recording the topology of the action.
why: Key tool for localization formulas and Schubert calculus; nLab page and one catalog result.

name: Equivariant K-theory
def: The K-theory built from $G$-equivariant vector bundles on a space with an action of a group $G$.
why: Underlies the Atiyah-Segal completion theorem and index theory; nLab page and one catalog result.

name: Euclidean space
def: The real vector space $\mathbb{R}^n$ with the standard inner product and the distance it induces.
why: The standard model space of geometry, analysis and physics; nLab page with 223 backlinks and one catalog result.

name: Forgetful functor
def: A functor that discards some structure, such as sending a group to its underlying set.
why: Standard device for free-forgetful adjunctions and monadicity; nLab page with 305 backlinks and one catalog result.

name: Grothendieck construction
def: The construction turning a functor $F: C\to\mathbf{Cat}$ into a fibered category whose objects are pairs $(c, x)$ with $x$ in $F(c)$.
why: Used in fibered-category and higher-categorical work; nLab page with 103 backlinks and one catalog result.

name: Group cohomology
def: The derived functors of taking invariants of $G$-modules, computed for example by the bar resolution.
why: Controls extensions (Schur-Zassenhaus) and feeds number theory and topology; nLab page and one catalog result.

name: Homotopy category
def: The category obtained by inverting weak equivalences or by passing to homotopy classes of maps.
why: Ground for Brown representability and derived/stable homotopy theory; nLab page with 203 backlinks.

name: Homotopy pullback
def: A pullback taken up to homotopy, invariant under replacing the diagram by a weakly equivalent one.
why: Standard tool of homotopy theory (Bousfield-Friedlander); nLab page with 205 backlinks; one catalog result.

name: Identity type
def: In dependent type theory, the type $a =_A b$ whose terms are proofs or paths that $a$ and $b$ of type $A$ are equal.
why: Core of homotopy type theory and proof assistants (Hedberg's theorem); nLab page with 146 backlinks.

name: Injection
def: A function that sends distinct inputs to distinct outputs.
why: An elementary notion used throughout mathematics (Cantor-Schroeder-Bernstein); nLab page with 158 backlinks.

name: Lawvere theory
def: A category with finite products whose objects are the powers of one object, presenting an algebraic theory.
why: Categorical form of universal algebra, used in computational effects semantics; nLab page and one catalog result.

name: Linear logic
def: A substructural logic, due to Girard, that drops weakening and contraction so that hypotheses are used exactly once.
why: Influential in proof theory and programming languages (resources, session types); nLab page with 192 backlinks and one result (Chu construction).

name: Locale
def: A frame (a complete lattice in which finite meets distribute over arbitrary joins) regarded as a generalized space without points.
why: Basic in constructive topology and topos theory (constructive Gelfand duality); nLab page; the word also has an everyday sense.
revised: tc-judge-revision/1: phrases narrowed after the first arXiv count showed everyday or other-field senses

name: Locally presentable category
def: A cocomplete category with a set of small objects that generates every object under filtered colimits.
why: A technical framework of category theory (Gabriel-Ulmer duality, model categories); nLab page and one catalog result.

name: Moduli stack
def: A stack whose points over a base classify families of geometric objects of a given type up to isomorphism, together with their automorphisms.
why: Central in modern algebraic geometry (moduli of curves, bundles); nLab page and one catalog result.

name: Monoid
def: A set with an associative binary operation and an identity element.
why: Appears in algebra, automata theory, category theory and programming; nLab page with 339 backlinks; Eckmann-Hilton in the catalog.

name: Natural isomorphism
def: A natural transformation between functors each of whose components is an isomorphism.
why: Expresses canonical identifications across mathematics (coherence theorem); nLab page with 263 backlinks.

name: Natural number
def: One of the numbers $0,1,2,3,\dots$ used for counting, characterized by zero and the successor operation.
why: The most basic number system, used everywhere; nLab page with 302 backlinks and induction in the catalog.

name: Operad
def: A collection of operations with $n$ inputs and one output for each $n$, with composition laws and symmetric-group actions encoding a type of algebra.
why: Organizes algebraic structures in homotopy theory and deformation quantization; nLab page with 172 backlinks and one result.

name: Orientation of a manifold
def: A consistent choice of orientation of all tangent spaces of a manifold, equivalently a choice of fundamental class.
why: Needed for integration (Stokes' theorem) and intersection theory; nLab page with 191 backlinks.

name: Power set
def: The set of all subsets of a given set.
why: Elementary and ubiquitous (Cantor's theorem); nLab page with 127 backlinks.

name: Pushout (category theory)
def: The colimit of a span $B\leftarrow A\to C$: a universal object receiving maps from $B$ and $C$ that agree on $A$.
why: Basic gluing construction (Blakers-Massey, van Kampen); nLab page with 196 backlinks.

name: Quasi-category
def: A simplicial set in which every inner horn has a filler, modelling an $(\infty,1)$-category.
why: Foundation of Lurie's higher category theory; nLab page and one catalog result.

name: Regular category
def: A finitely complete category with coequalizers of kernel pairs whose regular epimorphisms are stable under pullback.
why: Technical notion of categorical logic (Barr embedding theorem); nLab page and one catalog result.

name: Simplex
def: The convex hull of $n+1$ affinely independent points in Euclidean space.
why: Building block of triangulations, topology and optimization; nLab page with 145 backlinks; 'simplex' also names the simplex method.

name: Smash product
def: The quotient $X\times Y/(X\vee Y)$ of two pointed spaces, and its analogue for spectra.
why: Monoidal product of stable homotopy theory (Spanier-Whitehead duality); nLab page and one catalog result.

name: SU(2)
def: The group of $2\times2$ complex unitary matrices with determinant 1, homeomorphic to the 3-sphere.
why: Ubiquitous in quantum physics (spin, qubits; Solovay-Kitaev) and representation theory; nLab page and one result.

name: Linear subspace
def: A subset of a vector space closed under addition and scalar multiplication.
why: Basic linear algebra notion used in every applied field; nLab page and one catalog result.

name: Surjection
def: A function every element of whose codomain is the image of some input.
why: Elementary and ubiquitous (Cantor's theorem); nLab page with 128 backlinks.

name: Symmetric monoidal category
def: A monoidal category with natural isomorphisms $A\otimes B\cong B\otimes A$ that square to the identity and satisfy coherence.
why: Frames tensor products, TQFTs and quantum process theories; nLab page with 405 backlinks.

name: Symplectic manifold
def: A smooth manifold with a closed nondegenerate differential 2-form.
why: Phase spaces of classical mechanics and the basis of symplectic topology (non-squeezing); nLab page and one result.

name: Topological vector space
def: A vector space with a topology for which addition and scalar multiplication are continuous.
why: The general setting of functional analysis (Hahn-Banach separation); nLab page and one catalog result.

name: Topos
def: A category that behaves like the category of sets: finitely complete, cartesian closed, with a subobject classifier.
why: Unifies logic, geometry and set theory (constructive Gelfand duality); nLab page with 521 backlinks.

name: Twisted cohomology
def: Cohomology with coefficients in a local system, or more generally twisted by a class in a higher cohomology group.
why: Specialized invariant used in T-duality and hypergeometric integrals; nLab page and one catalog result.

name: Twisted K-theory
def: K-theory twisted by a degree-3 cohomology class, defined for example via bundles of Fredholm operators or gerbes.
why: Classifies D-brane charges and underlies topological T-duality; nLab page and one catalog result.

name: Univalence axiom
def: The axiom of homotopy type theory that the map from identifications of types to equivalences of types is itself an equivalence.
why: Defining axiom of univalent foundations (structure identity principle); nLab page with 103 backlinks.

name: Weak homotopy equivalence
def: A continuous map inducing isomorphisms on all homotopy groups at every basepoint.
why: Basic equivalence of homotopy theory (Whitehead theorem); nLab page with 223 backlinks.

name: ZFC
def: Zermelo-Fraenkel set theory with the axiom of choice, the standard first-order axiomatic foundation of mathematics.
why: The standard foundation; independence results like the continuum hypothesis are stated over it; nLab page.

name: Function
def: A rule assigning to each element of a domain set exactly one element of a codomain set.
why: The most basic notion of mathematics; nLab page with 587 backlinks (the packet's mathlib ContDiff is not a definition of function).

name: Cartesian product
def: The set of all ordered pairs $(a,b)$ with $a$ in $A$ and $b$ in $B$.
why: Elementary and used everywhere; nLab page with 371 backlinks.

name: Binary operation
def: A function that combines two elements of a set into one element of the same set.
why: Basic ingredient of every algebraic structure; judge's knowledge, no source record in the packet.

name: Total order
def: A partial order in which every two elements are comparable.
why: Basic order-theoretic notion appearing across mathematics and sorting algorithms; nLab page.

name: Subset
def: A set all of whose elements belong to another given set.
why: Elementary and used everywhere; nLab page with 366 backlinks.

name: Infinite set
def: A set that is not in bijection with $\{1,\dots,n\}$ for any natural number $n$.
why: Basic set-theoretic notion; nLab page and one catalog result.

name: Inverse function
def: A function $g$ that undoes $f$, so that $g(f(x))=x$ and $f(g(y))=y$.
why: Basic notion from school onwards (derivative of an inverse); nLab page and one catalog result.

name: Group homomorphism
def: A map $f$ between groups with $f(ab)=f(a)f(b)$ for all elements $a,b$.
why: Basic map of group theory (isomorphism theorems); two catalog results name it, no source record.

name: Ring homomorphism
def: A map between rings that preserves addition, multiplication and the multiplicative identity.
why: Basic map of ring theory (first isomorphism theorem); one catalog result.

name: Commutative ring
def: A ring whose multiplication is commutative.
why: Central object of commutative algebra and algebraic geometry; two catalog results name it.

name: Integral domain
def: A nonzero commutative ring with no zero divisors.
why: Standard class of rings in algebra and number theory; nLab page.

name: Quotient ring
def: The ring $R/I$ of cosets of an ideal $I$ in a ring $R$ with induced operations.
why: Basic construction (modular arithmetic, coding theory); nLab page and one catalog result.

name: Algebra over a field
def: A vector space over a field with a bilinear multiplication, usually assumed associative and unital.
why: Common frame of matrix, polynomial and group algebras; judge's knowledge only.

name: Root of a polynomial
def: A value $x$ at which a polynomial $p$ evaluates to zero, $p(x)=0$.
why: Elementary notion used from school algebra to numerical analysis; judge's knowledge only.

name: Linear functional
def: A linear map from a vector space to its field of scalars.
why: Basic to duality and functional analysis (Hahn-Banach); nLab page and one catalog result.

name: Rank of a matrix
def: The dimension of the column space of a matrix, equal to the maximal number of linearly independent columns.
why: Mathlib defines Matrix.rank; widely used in numerical linear algebra and machine learning (low-rank methods).

name: Orthogonality
def: The relation between two vectors whose inner product is zero, extended to subspaces and functions.
why: Used across geometry, Fourier analysis and signal processing; nLab page.

name: Hausdorff space
def: A topological space in which any two distinct points have disjoint open neighborhoods.
why: Mathlib defines T2Space and nLab has a page with 176 backlinks; standard separation axiom of topology.

name: Neighborhood (topology)
def: A set containing an open set that contains a given point.
why: Basic notion of topology and analysis; judge's knowledge only.

name: Closure (topology)
def: The smallest closed set containing a given subset of a topological space.
why: Basic topological operation; judge's knowledge only.

name: Interior (topology)
def: The largest open set contained in a given subset of a topological space.
why: Basic topological operation; judge's knowledge only.

name: Dense set
def: A subset of a topological space whose closure is the whole space.
why: Used for approximation arguments (Baire category theorem); two catalog results name it.

name: Limit of a function
def: The value $L$ that $f(x)$ approaches as $x$ approaches a point $a$, made precise by the $\varepsilon$-$\delta$ definition.
why: Foundation of calculus used everywhere; nLab page.

name: Differentiable function
def: A function that has a derivative at every point of its domain.
why: Central in analysis and all applied modelling; judge's knowledge only.

name: Riemann integral
def: The limit of Riemann sums of a function over finer and finer partitions of an interval.
why: The standard calculus integral (fundamental theorem of calculus); one catalog result.

name: Antiderivative
def: A function $F$ whose derivative is a given function $f$.
why: Basic calculus notion used in science and engineering; judge's knowledge only.

name: Gradient
def: The vector of partial derivatives of a scalar function, pointing in the direction of steepest increase.
why: Essential in optimization and machine learning (gradient descent); nLab page and one catalog result.

name: Ordinary differential equation
def: An equation relating an unknown function of one variable to its derivatives.
why: Models dynamics across science (Picard-Lindelof, Poincare-Bendixson); two catalog results and an nLab page.

name: Partial differential equation
def: An equation relating an unknown function of several variables to its partial derivatives.
why: Models physics and engineering; one catalog result (Cauchy-Kowalevski), no source record.

name: Tangent space
def: The vector space of tangent vectors (velocities of curves) at a point of a manifold.
why: Basic notion of differential geometry, used in robotics and optimization on manifolds; judge's knowledge only.

name: Tangent bundle
def: The disjoint union of all tangent spaces of a manifold, itself a manifold and a vector bundle.
why: Mathlib defines TangentBundle and nLab has a page with 216 backlinks; used in mechanics.

name: Measure space
def: A set with a sigma-algebra of measurable subsets and a measure on it.
why: Setting of integration and probability; nLab page.

name: Almost everywhere
def: Holding for all points outside a set of measure zero.
why: Standard qualifier in analysis and probability (Lebesgue differentiation); one catalog result.

name: Probability distribution
def: A description of how probability is assigned to the possible values of a random variable, formally a probability measure on its value space.
why: Fundamental across statistics, science and machine learning; nLab page.

name: Limit (category theory)
def: A universal cone over a diagram in a category, generalizing products, pullbacks and equalizers.
why: Central organizing notion of category theory; judge's knowledge only.

name: Universal property
def: A characterization of an object, up to unique isomorphism, by the maps into or out of it.
why: Pervasive method of definition (Lazard's theorem); one catalog result.

name: Product (category theory)
def: An object with projections to given objects through which every family of maps to them factors uniquely.
why: Basic universal construction generalizing cartesian products; judge's knowledge only.

name: Polygon
def: A plane figure bounded by a closed chain of finitely many straight line segments.
why: Basic geometric object, used in graphics and computational geometry (Pick's theorem); thin nLab page.

name: Path (graph theory)
def: A sequence of distinct vertices in a graph with each consecutive pair joined by an edge.
why: Basic graph notion used in routing and networks; judge's knowledge only.

name: Connected graph
def: A graph in which every two vertices are joined by a path.
why: Basic graph property used in networks and algorithms; thin nLab page.

name: Directed graph
def: A set of vertices with a set of ordered pairs of vertices called arcs.
why: Used in networks, automata and causal models (BEST theorem); nLab page.

name: Homomorphism
def: A map between algebraic structures of the same type that preserves their operations.
why: Fundamental across algebra; nLab page with 464 backlinks.
